I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾ ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces nor from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.﴾ ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿Say: "Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?" Rather, they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾ ﴿Or do they have gods that defend them from beside Us? They cannot help themselves, nor will they be companioned by Us.﴾:

al-Suddi and Muqatil said: The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by Abu Jahl and Abu Sufyan. Abu Jahl said: "This is the Prophet of Abd Manaf." Abu Sufyan said: "What do you find objectionable in him being a prophet among the Banu Abd Manaf?" The Messenger ﷺ heard them both and said to Abu Jahl: "You will not cease until there befalls you what befell your paternal uncle al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. As for you, Abu Sufyan, you only said what you said out of partisanship (hamiyyah)." Then this was revealed.

When the disbelievers were distressed by the mention of their gods in a bad light, they began to mock and belittle whoever mentioned them, as a form of retaliation. The (in) here is negating, with the meaning of (ma). The apparent view is that the answer to (idha) is ﴿in yattakhidhunaka﴾, and the answer to (idha) with the negating (in) does not occur in the Qur'an except in this verse and in His saying in the Qur'an ﴿When they see you, they take you only in mockery﴾ [al-Furqan: 41]. It did not need the (fa) in the answer, just as (ma) did not need it when it occurred as an answer, as in His saying: ﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them, their argument is nothing﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25]. This is unlike the particles of condition, for when the answer begins with the negating (ma), the (fa) is necessary, as in: "If you visit us, then we do not wrong you." In the answer of (idha) with the negating (in) and (ma) there is clear evidence that (idha) is not governed by the answer, but rather the verb that follows it is what governs it, and it is not a genitive construction attached to the clause, contrary to most grammarians. We have argued for this with other evidence in the commentary on al-Tashil.

It was also said: the answer to (idha) is omitted, and it is "they say," the quoted speech being their saying ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾, and His saying ﴿in yattakhidhunaka illa huzuwan﴾ is an interposed clause between (idha) and its answer. ﴿Yattakhidhunaka﴾ takes two objects, and the second, (huzuwan), means "a thing mocked at." This is an interrogative expressing denial and wonder. Remembrance (dhikr) can be by good or by evil; when its object is not mentioned, the context indicates it. If it comes from a friend it is praise, and if from others it is blame. Among its uses is ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60], meaning with evil. Likewise here: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾

Then He censured their denial of his mention of their gods by this circumstantial clause: ﴿And yet they are the ones who disbelieve in the mention of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning they deny. This is their condition: they disbelieve in the mention of the Most Merciful, which is what was sent down of the Qur'an. Whoever is in this condition should not object to one who disparages their gods. The apparent view is that this clause is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in ﴿yaqulun﴾, which is omitted.

Al-Zamakhshari said: the clause is in the position of a circumstantial clause, i.e., (they take you as a mockery) while they are in a state which is the root of mockery and derision, which is disbelief in God. End of quote. So he made the circumstantial clause's governing element (they take you as a mockery), omitted, and repeated them for emphasis. It is narrated that it was revealed when they denied the word "al-Rahman" and said: "We do not know al-Rahman except in Yamamah." The meaning of al-Rahman here is God, as if it was said: "and they, with the mention of God."

Since they were hastening God's punishment and His signs that compel acknowledgment and knowledge, God, exalted is He, forbade them from haste. He first mentioned the blame of man for excessive haste, and that he is naturally disposed to it. The apparent view is that "al-insan" here refers to the genus, and his being "created of haste" is by way of hyperbole, because it proceeds from him frequently, as one says to someone who plays a lot, "You are made of play." In a hadith: "I am not of the frivolous, nor is the frivolous of me." The poet said:

"Indeed we, when we strike the ram a blow on its head, the tongue flies out of its mouth."

Since they were people of striking skulls and constant war, he said that they are "of striking." With this interpretation the meaning of the verse is complete, and what follows from it is His saying: ﴿I will show you My signs﴾, i.e., the signs of threat, ﴿so do not seek to hasten them﴾ in seeing the punishment you hasten for.

As for one who claims there is inversion (qalb) in it, namely Abu Amr, and that the original is "the creation of haste from man," and likewise the reading of Abd Allah, in the sense that it was made a nature of his natures and a part of his character, this view is not good, because inversion in sound speech is not proper, and its domain is poetry. It was said: among what occurs in speech of this kind is the Arab saying: "When Sirius rises, the wood is level over the chameleon." And they said: "The she-camel was presented to the pool." And in poetry his saying:

"I stripped my hand from the garment, taking hold of it."

Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said that "al-insan" here is Adam. Mujahid said: When the spirit entered his head and eyes, he saw the sun approaching sunset, and said: "My Lord, hasten the completion of my creation before the sun sets." Sa'id said: When the spirit reached his knees, he nearly stood up, and God said: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾. Ibn Zayd said: God created him on Friday with haste in his creation. Al-Akhfash said: ﴿of haste﴾ because God said to him "Be," and he was. Al-Hasan said: ﴿of haste﴾ means weak, meaning the drop of semen. It was said: he was created swiftly and hastily, not in the order of the sons of Adam from drop, clot and lump; this returns to al-Akhfash's view. It was said: ﴿of haste﴾ means of clay, and "ajal" in the dialect of Himyar means clay. Abu Ubaydah recited for one of the Himyarites:

"The wood in the hard rock, its place of growth; and the palm, its place of growth is in water and clay."

It was said: "al-insan" here is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. The view that the verse should be understood as referring to him is the first view, which is the one that suits its ending. As for "the signs" here, it was said: the swift destruction in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter, i.e., it will come to you at its time. It was said: the proofs of monotheism and the truthfulness of the Messenger. It was said: the traces of past generations in al-Sham and Yemen. The first view is most fitting, i.e., what will distress you will come if you persist in your disbelief, as if he means the Day of Badr and other things in this world and in the Hereafter.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why did He forbid them from hastening when He said ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ and ﴿And man has been ever hasty﴾ [al-Isra': 11]? Is this not imposing what cannot be borne? I say: this is like the desire that was placed in him, and He commanded him to overcome it, because He gave him the power by which he can suppress desire and abandon haste. End of quote. This is in the way of the Mu'tazilah.

Mujahid, Humayd and Ibn Miqsam read (khalaqa) in the active voice, with (al-insana) in the accusative, meaning God created man. His saying ﴿When is this promise?﴾ is an interrogative in the manner of mockery, and the Muslims used to threaten them on the tongue of the Law. (Mata) is in the position of a genitive for this, so its position is nominative. It is reported from some Kufans that the position of (mata) is accusative as an adverb of time, governed by an implied verb whose estimate is "it will be" or "it will come." The answer of (law) is omitted, for the context indicates it, and omitting it is more eloquent and awe-inspiring than stating it. Ibn Atiyyah estimated it as "when they hasten and the like," and al-Zamakhshari estimated it as "when they were in that state of disbelief, mockery and hastening." It was also said: "they would have known the truth of resurrection." It was said: "they would have known the truth of the promised thing." Al-Hawfi said: "they would have hastened to faith." Al-Kisa'i said: it is an alert to the certainty of the occurrence of the Hour, and (hin), when it is meant as the time of the Hour, indicates this, in ﴿but it will come upon them suddenly﴾. End of quote.

(Hin) — al-Zamakhshari said: it is an object of (ya'lamu), i.e., "if they knew the time which they hasten about by their saying ﴿When is this promise?﴾, which is a time hard and severe, the fire encompassing them from behind and in front, but their ignorance of it is what made it light in their estimation." He said: It is also possible that (ya'lamu) is left without an object, meaning "if they had knowledge and were not ignorant, they would not have been hasty," and (hin) is governed by an implied verb, i.e., ﴿when they will not ward off from their faces the Fire﴾ they will know that they were upon falsehood, and this great ignorance will be removed from them, i.e., they will not ward it off. End of quote. What appears to be the case is that the object of (ya'lamu) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e., "if those who disbelieve knew the coming of the promised thing which they asked about and sought to deduce." (Hin) is governed by the object, which is "coming," and it is possible that it is of the type of the "working" (i'mal) construction with an omitted modifier, and the second is made to work, the meaning being "if they knew the direct contact of the Fire when they will not ward it off from their faces." He mentioned the faces because they are the noblest part of man and the seat of his senses, and man is most eager to defend them among his limbs. Then he joined to them the backs. The meaning is the generality of the Fire over all their bodies, and no one will prevent them from the punishment. ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., it will startle them. Ibn Atiyyah said: ﴿Rather, it will come upon them﴾ is a transition (istidrak) preceded by an implied negation, its estimate being: "Indeed the signs do not come according to their demands." End of quote. The apparent view is that the pronoun in (ta'tihim) refers to the Fire. It was said: it refers to the Hour that will bring them to punishment. It was said: to the punishment. Al-Zamakhshari said: regarding the return of the pronoun to the Fire, or to the promise, because it means the Fire which they promised, or on the interpretation of the promise and the pledge, or to the (hin), because it means the Hour, or to the sending of the Messenger. End of quote.

Al-A'mash read (bal ya'tihim) with the yā', (baghtatan) with fatha on the ghayn, (fayabhutuhum) with the yā', and the pronoun refers to the promise or the (hin), as al-Zamakhshari said. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi said: perhaps he made the Fire mean the punishment, so he mentioned it, then returned the pronoun (radduha) to the apparent wording. ﴿And they will not be given respite﴾, i.e., they will not be delayed from what has befallen them.

When His saying ﴿When they take you only in mockery﴾ preceded, God consoled him that those who came before him among the messengers were also mocked by their peoples, and that the fruit of their mockery was ripe destruction and punishment in this world and the Hereafter; so likewise is the state of these mockers. The explanation of a verse like this has preceded in al-An'am.

Then God commanded him to ask them: who protects you at your times from the might of God, i.e., no one protects you from it. This is an interrogative of rebuke and reproach. At the end of the speech there is an omitted estimate, as if they had no preventer and no guardian. On this negation is the construction of (bal) in His saying ﴿Rather, they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord﴾, as Ibn Atiyyah said. Al-Zamakhshari said: Rather, they are turning away from His remembrance, not bringing it to mind, let alone fearing His might, until when they are granted protection from Him they recognize who the guardian is and become fit to be asked about Him. The meaning is that He commanded His Messenger to ask them about the guardian, then He made clear that they are not fit for that, because of their turning away from the remembrance of the One who guards them. End of quote.

Abu Ja'far, al-Zuhri and Shaybah read (yaklukum) with a light damma and without hamza. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' recounted (yaklawkum) with fatha on the lam and sukun on the waw.

﴿Or do they have gods﴾, with the meaning of "rather", and the interrogative hamzah, as if it were said: "Rather, do they have gods...?" He turned away from the first statement and then asked a question. ﴿That can prevent them﴾ from the punishment. Al-Hawfi said: ﴿besides Us﴾ is connected to ﴿can prevent them﴾. End of quote. It was said: the meaning is, "Do they have gods that make them secure and protected from anything disagreeable reaching them from Our side?"

Ibn ʿAbbas said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech. Its implied sense is: "Or do they have, besides Us, gods that can prevent them?" One says: "I prevented harm from him" (mana'tu dunahu), meaning, "I warded off his harm." So ﴿besides Us﴾ is connected either to ﴿gods﴾, meaning, "Or do they have gods other than Us?", or to ﴿can prevent them﴾, meaning, "Or do they have a protector other than Us?" Then he began a new statement about their gods, clarifying that what is not able to help itself or prevent harm, and is not accompanied by God with support and aid, how could it prevent and help others?

Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿they will be accompanied﴾ means "they will be prevented." Mujahid said: "they will be helped." Qatadah said: "they will not be accompanied by any good from God." The poet said:

He calls out with the highest of his voice, seeking refuge,
so that he may be accompanied by us, while the spears are hostile.

Mujahid said: "they will be guarded." Al-Suddi said: "none of the angels will accompany them to repel [harm] from them."

The apparent meaning is that the pronoun in ﴿their protector﴾ [al-Baqarah: 142] refers to the idols, and this is the view of Qatadah. It was also said that it refers to the disbelievers, and this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. In al-Tahrir, the discussion of this word, namely ﴿yusḥabūn﴾, depends on two meanings. One is that it derives from ṣaḥiba, yaṣḥabu. The second is from al-iṣhāb: aṣḥaba al-rajul, meaning he protected the man from calamities.

He said: It is also possible that (ya'lamu) is left without an object, meaning "if they had knowledge and were not ignorant, they would not have been hasty," and (hin) is governed by an implied verb, i.e., ﴿when they will not ward off from their faces the Fire﴾ they will know that they were upon falsehood, and this great ignorance will be removed from them, i.e., they will not ward it off. End of quote. What appears to be the case is that the object of (ya'lamu) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e., "if those who disbelieve knew the coming of the promised thing which they asked about and sought to deduce." (Hin) is governed by the object, which is "coming," and it is possible that it is of the type of the "working" (i'mal) construction with an omitted modifier, and the second is made to work, the meaning being "if they knew the direct contact of the Fire when they will not ward it off from their faces." He mentioned the faces because they are the noblest part of man and the seat of his senses, and man is most eager to defend them among his limbs. Then he joined to them the backs. The meaning is the generality of the Fire over all their bodies, and no one will prevent them from the punishment. ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., it will startle them. Ibn Atiyyah said: ﴿Rather, it will come upon them﴾ is a transition (istidrak) preceded by an implied negation, its estimate being: "Indeed the signs do not come according to their demands." End of quote. The apparent view is that the pronoun in (ta'tihim) refers to the Fire. It was said: it refers to the Hour that will bring them to punishment. It was said: to the punishment. Al-Zamakhshari said: regarding the return of the pronoun to the Fire, or to the promise, because it means the Fire which they promised, or on the interpretation of the promise and the pledge, or to the (hin), because it means the Hour, or to the sending of the Messenger. End of quote.

Al-A'mash read (bal ya'tihim) with the yā', (baghtatan) with fatha on the ghayn, (fayabhutuhum) with the yā', and the pronoun refers to the promise or the (hin), as al-Zamakhshari said. When His saying ﴿When they take you only in mockery﴾ preceded, God consoled him that those who came before him among the messengers were also mocked by their peoples, and that the fruit of their mockery was ripe destruction and punishment in this world and the Hereafter; so likewise is the state of these mockers. The explanation of a verse like this has preceded in al-An'am.

Then God commanded him to ask them: who protects you at your times from the might of God, i.e., no one protects you from it. This is an interrogative of rebuke and reproach. At the end of the speech there is an omitted estimate, as if they had no preventer and no guardian. End of quote.

Abu Ja'far, al-Zuhri and Shaybah read (yaklukum) with a light damma and without hamza. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' recounted (yaklawkum) with fatha on the lam and sukun on the waw.

﴿Or do they have gods﴾, with the meaning of "rather", and the interrogative hamzah, as if it were said: "Rather, do they have gods...?" It was said: the meaning is, "Do they have gods that make them secure and protected from anything disagreeable reaching them from Our side?"

He calls out with the highest of his voice, seeking refuge,
so that he may be accompanied by us, while the spears are hostile.

Mujahid said: "they will be guarded." Al-Suddi said: "none of the angels will accompany them to repel [harm] from them."

It was also said that it refers to the disbelievers, and this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. In al-Tahrir, the discussion of this word, namely ﴿yusḥabūn﴾, depends on two meanings. One is that it derives from ṣaḥiba, yaṣḥabu. The second is from al-iṣhāb: aṣḥaba al-rajul, meaning he protected the man from calamities.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 21, verse 36–43 (part 1 of 2):

(p-312) ﴿When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in mockery: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" And yet they are the ones who disbelieve in the mention of the Most Merciful.﴾ ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾ ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces nor from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.﴾ ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿Say: "Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?" Rather, they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾ ﴿Or do they have gods that defend them from beside Us? They cannot help themselves, nor will they be companioned by Us.﴾:

al-Suddi and Muqatil said: The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by Abu Jahl and Abu Sufyan. Abu Jahl said: "This is the Prophet of Abd Manaf." Abu Sufyan said: "What do you find objectionable in him being a prophet among the Banu Abd Manaf?" The Messenger ﷺ heard them both and said to Abu Jahl: "You will not cease until there befalls you what befell your paternal uncle al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. As for you, Abu Sufyan, you only said what you said out of partisanship (hamiyyah)." Then this was revealed.

The (in) here is negating, with the meaning of (ma). The apparent view is that the answer to (idha) is ﴿in yattakhidhunaka﴾, and the answer to (idha) with the negating (in) does not occur in the Qur'an except in this verse and in His saying in the Qur'an ﴿When they see you, they take you only in mockery﴾ [al-Furqan: 41]. It did not need the (fa) in the answer, just as (ma) did not need it when it occurred as an answer, as in His saying: ﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them, their argument is nothing﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25]. This is unlike the particles of condition, for when the answer begins with the negating (ma), the (fa) is necessary, as in: "If you visit us, then we do not wrong you." In the answer of (idha) with the negating (in) and (ma) there is clear evidence that (idha) is not governed by the answer, but rather the verb that follows it is what governs it, and it is not a genitive construction attached to the clause, contrary to most grammarians. We have argued for this with other evidence in the commentary on al-Tashil.

It was also said: the answer to (idha) is omitted, and it is "they say," the quoted speech being their saying ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾, and His saying ﴿in yattakhidhunaka illa huzuwan﴾ is an interposed clause between (idha) and its answer. ﴿Yattakhidhunaka﴾ takes two objects, and the second, (huzuwan), means "a thing mocked at." This is an interrogative expressing denial and wonder. Remembrance (dhikr) can be by good or by evil; when its object is not mentioned, the context indicates it. If it comes from a friend it is praise, and if from others it is blame. Among its uses is ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60], meaning with evil. Likewise here: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾

Then He censured their denial of his mention of their gods by this circumstantial clause: ﴿And yet they are the ones who disbelieve in the mention of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning they deny. This is their condition: they disbelieve in the mention of the Most Merciful, which is what was sent down of the Qur'an. Whoever is in this condition should not object to one who disparages their gods. The apparent view is that this clause is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in ﴿yaqulun﴾, which is omitted.

Al-Zamakhshari said: the clause is in the position of a circumstantial clause, i.e., (they take you as a mockery) while they are in a state which is the root of mockery and derision, which is disbelief in God. It is narrated that it was revealed when they denied the word "al-Rahman" and said: "We do not know al-Rahman except in Yamamah." The meaning of al-Rahman here is God, as if it was said: "and they, with the mention of God."

Since they were hastening God's punishment and His signs that compel acknowledgment and knowledge, God, exalted is He, forbade them from haste. He first mentioned the blame of man for excessive haste, and that he is naturally disposed to it. The apparent view is that "al-insan" here refers to the genus, and his being "created of haste" is by way of hyperbole, because it proceeds from him frequently, as one says to someone who plays a lot, "You are made of play." Since they were people of striking skulls and constant war, he said that they are "of striking." The first view is most fitting, i.e., what will distress you will come if you persist in your disbelief, as if he means the Day of Badr and other things in this world and in the Hereafter.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 21, verses 44–50:**

[p. 315] ﴿Nay, We gave enjoyment to these people and their fathers until life stretched long over them. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? Are they the victors?﴾ ﴿Say: "I only warn you by revelation," but the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.﴾ ﴿And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord touches them, they will surely say, "Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿We shall set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in anything. Even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We shall bring it. And We suffice as reckoners.﴾ ﴿And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, a light and a reminder for the God-fearing,﴾ ﴿who fear their Lord in the unseen and are apprehensive of the Hour.﴾ ﴿And this is a blessed reminder that We have sent down. Will you then deny it?﴾

﴿These people﴾ refers to those addressed before, namely the disbelievers of Quraysh and those who took gods besides God. God informs that He gave ﴿these people﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿and their fathers﴾ before them, provision from the fleeting goods of this world, until their lives lengthened in ease and comfort. They stumbled into misguidance because of His giving them respite and delaying them until the time when He would seize them. ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? Are they the victors?﴾ The explanation of this sentence has already been given at the end of Surah al-Ra'd. Al-Zamakhshari (d. 538 AH) limited himself among those interpretations to the meaning that We reduce the land of unbelief and the abode of war, and remove its outlying parts by empowering the Muslims over it, giving them victory over its people, and returning it to the abode of Islam. He said: "If you ask, what is the benefit in His saying ﴿We come to the land﴾? I say: the benefit in it is depicting what God was making happen at the hands of the Muslims, and that their armies and detachments were raiding the land of the polytheists and coming to it victorious over it, having reduced it from its outlying parts." End of quotation.

In this there is good news for the believers of what God will open for them. Most of the exegetes hold that the verse was revealed about the disbelievers of Makkah. Their saying ﴿Are they the victors?﴾ is evidence of this, since the meaning is that they are the victors. It is an interrogative of rebuke and reproach, since they did not take heed from what was happening to them.

Then God commanded him to say: ﴿I only warn you by revelation﴾, meaning: I inform you of what you fear by a revelation from God, not from my own opinion. What comes from God is the truth that certainly occurs, as you have seen with your own eyes in the reduction of the land from its outlying parts. Then He informed that they, despite being warned, turn away from what they were warned of. Thus warning is of no benefit to them, since they are deaf to hearing it. Since revelation is among the things heard, mentioning deafness is appropriate. ﴿The deaf﴾ are those who are warned. The article ﴿al-﴾ here is for the known (al-'ahd), and the apparent noun has taken the place of the pronoun, because it explicitly states their deafness and the stopping of their ears when they are warned. The pronoun would not have conveyed this meaning. The negation of hearing here is the negation of its benefit.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿yasma'u﴾ with a fatha on the ya' and the mim, with ﴿al-summu﴾ in the nominative as its subject and ﴿al-du'a'a﴾ in the accusative as its object. Ibn 'Amir, Ibn Jubayr on the authority of Abu 'Amr, and Ibn al-Salt on the authority of Hafs read it with a ta' above, damma on it, and kasra on the mim: ﴿al-summu al-du'a'a﴾ with both in the accusative, and the subject is the pronoun of the addressee, who is the Messenger (ﷺ). Another reading is the same except with a ya' below, meaning ﴿and does not hear﴾, i.e., the Messenger. It is also transmitted from him (ﷺ) as ﴿wa-la yusma'u﴾ in the passive, with ﴿al-summu﴾ in the nominative as its agent, reported by Ibn Khalawayh. Ahmad ibn Jubayr al-Antaki transmitted from al-Yazidi on the authority of Abu 'Amr [p. 316] ﴿yusmi'u﴾ with damma on the ya' and kasra on the mim, ﴿al-summa﴾ in the accusative, and ﴿al-du'a'u﴾ in the nominative as its subject. The verb is attributed to ﴿al-du'a'﴾ figuratively (ittisa'an), and the second object is omitted, as if it were said: "the calling does not make the deaf hear anything."

Then God informed that these people, who were deaf to hearing what they were warned of, when something of what they were warned of reaches them, even if it is small, they call out for destruction and confess that they were wrongdoers. They were alerted to the cause that necessitated punishment for them, which is the wrongdoing of disbelief, and they were humbled and submitted.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿nafhah﴾ is a portion, and it is also said that it is the hunger that came down upon Makkah. Ibn Jurayj said: a share, from the saying "nafaha lahu min al-'ata'," when one gives him a portion. In His saying ﴿if a breath touches them﴾ there are three emphases: the word "touch", and what is implied by "nafh" of paucity, since it is a light wind or what is given as a small portion, and the form of the single occurrence (al-marrah) derived from it, though "nafh" itself is not used. The meaning is that with the slightest contact of the least punishment they submitted, humbled themselves, and confessed that the cause of that was their earlier wrongdoing.

When He mentioned their state in this world, when they are afflicted with something, He digressed (istatrada) to what will happen in the Hereafter, which is the abode of reward and punishment. He informed about His justice and attributed that to Himself with the plural of majesty, saying ﴿We shall set up the scales﴾. The discussion of the scales has already been presented at the beginning of al-A'raf. People differ about this: is there a real scale, which is the view of the majority, or is it a figurative expression of the extreme perfection of complete justice, which is the view of al-Dahhak and Qatadah? They both said: there is no scale, but it is justice, and ﴿al-qist﴾ is a verbal noun by which the scales are described, as an intensification, as if they were made to be justice in themselves. Or it is by omission of a modifier, meaning "possessors of ﴿justice﴾". It is also permissible that it be an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), meaning for the sake of ﴿justice﴾.

Apparently ﴿hasibin﴾ is a specification (tamyiz) since it accepts ﴿min﴾, and it may also be a circumstantial state (hal).

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 21, verses 44–50:**

Are they the victors?﴾ ﴿Say: "I only warn you by revelation," but the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.﴾ ﴿And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord touches them, they will surely say, "Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿We shall set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in anything. Even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We shall bring it. And We suffice as reckoners.﴾ ﴿And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, a light and a reminder for the God-fearing,﴾ ﴿who fear their Lord in the unseen and are apprehensive of the Hour.﴾ ﴿And this is a blessed reminder that We have sent down. Will you then deny it?﴾

﴿These people﴾ refers to those addressed before, namely the disbelievers of Quraysh and those who took gods besides God. God informs that He gave ﴿these people﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿and their fathers﴾ before them, provision from the fleeting goods of this world, until their lives lengthened in ease and comfort. They stumbled into misguidance because of His giving them respite and delaying them until the time when He would seize them. ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? Are they the victors?﴾ The explanation of this sentence has already been given at the end of Surah al-Ra'd. Al-Zamakhshari (d. 538 AH) limited himself among those interpretations to the meaning that We reduce the land of unbelief and the abode of war, and remove its outlying parts by empowering the Muslims over it, giving them victory over its people, and returning it to the abode of Islam. He said: "If you ask, what is the benefit in His saying ﴿We come to the land﴾? I say: the benefit in it is depicting what God was making happen at the hands of the Muslims, and that their armies and detachments were raiding the land of the polytheists and coming to it victorious over it, having reduced it from its outlying parts." End of quotation.

In this there is good news for the believers of what God will open for them. Most of the exegetes hold that the verse was revealed about the disbelievers of Makkah. Their saying ﴿Are they the victors?﴾ is evidence of this, since the meaning is that they are the victors. It is an interrogative of rebuke and reproach, since they did not take heed from what was happening to them.

Then God commanded him to say: ﴿I only warn you by revelation﴾, meaning: I inform you of what you fear by a revelation from God, not from my own opinion. Since revelation is among the things heard, mentioning deafness is appropriate. ﴿The deaf﴾ are those who are warned. The article ﴿al-﴾ here is for the known (al-'ahd), and the apparent noun has taken the place of the pronoun, because it explicitly states their deafness and the stopping of their ears when they are warned. The pronoun would not have conveyed this meaning. The negation of hearing here is the negation of its benefit.

Another reading is the same except with a ya' below, meaning ﴿and does not hear﴾, i.e., the Messenger. It is also transmitted from him (ﷺ) as ﴿wa-la yusma'u﴾ in the passive, with ﴿al-summu﴾ in the nominative as its agent, reported by Ibn Khalawayh. Then God informed that these people, who were deaf to hearing what they were warned of, when something of what they were warned of reaches them, even if it is small, they call out for destruction and confess that they were wrongdoers. They were alerted to the cause that necessitated punishment for them, which is the wrongdoing of disbelief, and they were humbled and submitted.

It is read as ﴿al-qisti﴾ with a sad. The lam in ﴿li-yawm al-qiyamah﴾: al-Zamakhshari said: it is like it in your saying, "I came for five nights passed of the month." From it is the verse of al-Nabighah:

The meaning is that nothing of their deeds is hidden from Us. It has also been said that it is a metaphor for requital. Apparently ﴿hasibin﴾ is a specification (tamyiz) since it accepts ﴿min﴾, and it may also be a circumstantial state (hal).

When He mentioned what His Messenger brought of the reminder and the state of the polytheists of the Arabs with him, and said ﴿Say: "I only warn you by revelation"﴾, He followed it with the fact that this is God's custom with His prophets. So He mentioned what He gave ﴿Moses and Aaron﴾, an indication of their story with their people, along with what they were given of the Criterion, the light, and the reminder. Then He alerted to what He gave His Messenger (ﷺ) of the blessed reminder, then asked, in the form of a reminder, about their denial, then again alerted to what He gave His Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿The Criterion﴾ is the Torah, and it is the light. And "the reminder" means a book which is a criterion, a light, and a reminder. This meaning is supported by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak: ﴿diya'an wa-dhikran﴾ without a waw before "diya'." Another group said: the Qur'an is what God gave of His help, the manifestation of His proof, and other things that distinguished His command from the command of Pharaoh. The light is the Torah, and the reminder is admonition and exhortation, or the mention of what they need in their religion and their interests, or nobility. The conjunction with waw indicates difference.

From Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿al-Furqan﴾ is "the victory," based on His saying ﴿the Day of the Criterion﴾. From al-Dahhak: the agitation of the sea. From Muhammad ibn Ka'b: that which delivers from doubts. ﴿Alladhina﴾ is a following attribute, or a separate clause in the nominative, accusative, or as an appositive. When He mentioned God-fearingness, He mentioned what it produces, which is the fear of God and apprehension of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The Hour﴾ is the Resurrection, and ﴿in the unseen﴾ means: the majority said they fear Him though they have not seen Him. Muqatil said: they fear His punishment though they have not seen it. Al-Zajjaj said: they fear Him from where no one sees them, and Ibn 'Attiyah preferred this. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi said: they fear Him when they are out of people's sight. Ishfaq (apprehension) is intense fear. It is possible that His saying ﴿and they are apprehensive of the Hour﴾ is a new informative statement about them, and it is possible that it is conjoined to the relative clause of ﴿alladhina﴾. In that case the first relative clause indicates constant renewal, as though it refers to their conduct regarding worldly matters, and the second relative clause, consisting of a subject and predicate with the nominal form that indicates the established quality, is as though it refers to their state regarding the Hereafter.

When He mentioned what He gave Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, He pointed to what He gave Muhammad (ﷺ), saying ﴿and this﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a blessed reminder﴾, meaning its benefits are abundant and its news is rich. Here the description came first with a noun, then with a sentence, following the more famous usage. The explanation of His saying in al-An'am ﴿And this is a blessed Book that We have sent down﴾ [al-An'am 6:92] has already been given, and there the wisdom of placing the sentence before the noun was explained. ﴿Will you then deny it?﴾ is an interrogative of denial and reproach, addressed to the polytheists. The pronoun in ﴿la-hu﴾ refers to ﴿reminder﴾, which is the Qur'an. In it is consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) when the polytheists deny it, just as the ancestors of the Jews denied what God sent down to Moses, peace be upon him.

(p. 318)﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾ ﴿They said, "Who has done this to our gods? He is surely among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 59] ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60] ﴿They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 61] ﴿They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 62] ﴿He said, "Rather, this one, their chief, did it. So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63] ﴿So they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 64] ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads: "You know well that these do not speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 65] ﴿He said, "Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 66] ﴿"Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not reason?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 67] ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 68] ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69] ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 70] ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 71] ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made each of them righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72] ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah, and they were worshippers of Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73] ﴿And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that used to commit wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 74] ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 75] ﴿And Noah, when he called out before; so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76] ﴿And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 77] ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field into which the sheep of a people had strayed at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78] ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with David, and the birds too, and We were the doers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 79] ﴿And We taught him the making of armor for you, to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 80] ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, running by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 81] ﴿And among the devils were those who dove for him and did other work besides that. And We were its guardians.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 82] ﴿And Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 83] ﴿So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity, and We gave him his family and the like thereof with them, as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 84] ﴿And Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl, each of them was among the patient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 85] ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 86] ﴿And Dhun-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree against him, then called out in the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87] ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 88] ﴿And Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 89] ﴿So We responded to him, gave him John, and made his wife fit for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, call upon Us in hope and fear, and were humbly submissive to Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90] ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91] ﴿Indeed, this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 92] ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects; each to Us will be returning.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 93] ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We are recording it for him.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 94] ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a city which We have destroyed that they will not return.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95] ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they will be swarming from every elevation.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 96] ﴿And the true promise has drawn near, and at once the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror. "O woe to us! We were in heedlessness of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 97] ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving thereto.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98] ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, but all will abide therein eternally.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 99] ﴿For them therein is a groaning, and they will not hear therein.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 100] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101] ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide eternally in what their souls desire.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 102] ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying, "This is your day, which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103] ﴿On the day We will fold up the heaven like the rolling up of the written scroll for documents. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will be doing it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104] ﴿And We had certainly written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105] ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 106] ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107] ﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God, so will you submit?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108] ﴿And if they turn away, say, "I have announced to you equally, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or distant."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109] ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and knows what you conceal.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 110] ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 111] ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you describe."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 112]

al-Timthal: the made image, a form resembling one of Allah's created beings. One says "mathaltu al-shay' bi al-shay'" when one likens one thing to another. The poet said:

"And how many a day have I spent in pleasure, and a night, with a maiden whose slender form was like the line of a statue."

Al-Jadhdh: cutting off. The poet said:

"The sons of al-Muhallab, may Allah cut off their root, have become ashes, leaving neither root nor branch."

Al-Naks: turning a thing over so that its top becomes its bottom. "Nakkasa ra'sahu," with shadda or without, means he lowered his head until its top became its bottom. Al-Bard: the verbal noun of barada. It is said, "barrada al-ma' harārat al-jawf yubarriduha" (water cools the heat of the stomach). The poet said:

(p. 319) "He left my she-camel idle among the saddle-camels, and she will cool hearts and make the weepers weep."

Al-Nafsh: the grazing of livestock at night without a shepherd, and the wandering of them by day without a shepherd. Al-Ghawṣ: entering under water to extract what is in it. The poet said:

"Or a Sadafite pearl whose diver is joyful; whenever he sees it, he cries out and prostrates."

Al-Nūn: the fish, plural "ninan." It is also narrated that "al-ninan" precedes it, "al-humr." Al-Farj: it is applied to the free (the front), the male as opposed to the female, and to the rear. The poet said:

"And you, when you turned your back on him, he tightened his rear, raised above the ground and not weak."

Al-Hadab: a raised part of the ground, like a mountain, a mound, a grave, and the like. Al-Nasalan: quick walking with haste. The poet said:

"The wolf's swift pace has become near, when the night grew cold upon it, so it hastened."

Al-Haṣab: firewood in the Abyssinian language. When it is thrown into the fire, before it is thrown it is not called haṣab. It is said: the haṣab is what fire is kindled with. Al-Sijill: the record, the document.

﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾.

When the discourse had preceded regarding the proofs of Tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and the return (ma'ad), He followed that with thirteen prophets, without observing chronological order in mentioning them. He also mentioned some of the trials that many of them endured, all of this as consolation to the Messenger ﷺ, and so that he might take them as an example regarding what befell him from his people.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited ﴿rushdahu﴾ with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the shin. 'Isa al-Thaqafi recited "rashadahu" with a fatha on the ra' and the shin, and he attributed the rushd to Ibrahim, meaning it is the rushd of one like him, which is the rushd of the prophets, and it has a great status. Rushd means prophethood and guidance to the ways of righteousness in religion and worldly affairs. Or both are included under rushd. Or the Sahifah and wisdom, or receiving success in good from childhood. There are five opinions. The object of the preposition is from a deleted antecedent, and it is definite, which is why "qabl" is indeclinable: that is, from before Musa and Harun. This was said by al-Dahhak, like His saying in al-An'am: ﴿And Noah, We guided before﴾ [al-An'am: 84], meaning before Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob. He who went to the view that the implied meaning is "before his reaching puberty," or "before his prophethood," meaning when he was in the loins of Adam and the covenant of the prophets was taken, is a far-fetched view. Or before Muhammad ﷺ, because these are deleted elements with no evidence indicating their deletion, unlike "from before" Musa and Harun, since they were mentioned previously. And its nearness. The pronoun in "bihi" most apparently refers to Ibrahim. It was said: it refers to rushd. Allah, exalted is He, informed that He knew from him wondrous states and marvelous secrets, so He qualified him for His intimate friendship (khullah), like His saying: "Allah knows best where to place His messages." This is one of the greatest and most eloquent praises, since Allah, exalted is He, informed that He gave him rushd and that He knew what He had given him, upon him be peace.

Then he digressed from that to explaining rushd, which is calling to the oneness of Allah and rejecting what is worshipped besides Him. "Idh" is governed either by "ataynā" or by "rushdahu" and "ʿālimīn," or by a deleted element, meaning: mention the time of his rushd, this moment. He began first with mentioning his father, because he was the most important in his advice and in rescuing him from error. Then he joined "his people" to it, like His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214]. In His saying ﴿What are these statues﴾ there is a belittling of them, a diminishing of their status, and a feigned ignorance about them, despite his knowledge of them and of their veneration by them. In his address to them with "antum" (you) there is contempt for them and a reproach over their wicked conduct. "ʿAkafa" is transitive with "ʿalā," like His saying: ﴿They cling to idols they have﴾ [al-A'raf: 138]. So it was said that "la-hā" here means "ʿalay-hā," as it was said in His saying: ﴿And if you do evil, it is to yourselves﴾ [al-Isra': 7]. The apparent meaning is that the lam in "la-hā" is the lam of causation, meaning "for its veneration," and the complement of ﴿ʿākifūn﴾ is deleted, meaning "upon its worship." It was said: ʿākifūn has been made to imply the meaning of ʿābidūn, so it takes the lam.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He did not intend a deleted object for "al-ʿākifīn," and he treated it as an intransitive verb, like His saying "fāʿilūn al-ʿukūf lahā" (doers of the devotion to it), or "wāqifūn lahā" (standing before it). End of quote.

When he questioned them, they answered with mere **taqlid** (blind imitation, *taqlid* being the uncritical following of others) and said that it was the practice of their fathers, so they followed it without any proof. How ugly is this taqlid, which led them to worship wood, stone and metal. Their obstinacy in this matter, and their defence of their imitation, is also clear. His question about worshipping the images had the aim that they would mention some doubt about it, so that he could refute it. When they answered him with something in which they had no doubt-based justification, and their misguidance became evident, ﴿He said: "You and your fathers have certainly been in clear error."﴾ That is, in obvious bewilderment with no ambiguity in it. He judged that both the imitators and those imitated were in error, and he made the error settled for them. The word "you" (*antum*) is an emphatic pronoun for the pronoun that is the subject of "were" (*kana*).

Al-Zamakhshari said: "*Antum* belongs to the kind of emphasis without which the sentence is not sound, because coordinating (*'atf*) upon the pronoun in *huwa* is, in the judgement of the grammarians, like part of the verb, and is therefore impermissible, and similar to it is ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35]." End of quote.

This is not a unanimously agreed ruling, so the sentence is not invalid without it, because the Kufans permit coordinating upon the attached nominative pronoun without emphasis by a detached nominative pronoun and without a separating element. His comparison of this with ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ contradicts his own position on ﴿Dwell, you and your wife﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35], since he claims that "and your wife" is not coordinated upon the concealed pronoun in "dwell" but rather that "and your wife" is nominative by an implied element, meaning "let [your wife] dwell". Thus, according to him, it is a coordination of sentences. This claim contradicts the school of Sibawayh.

When this question and answer had occurred, they were astonished at his misleading them, since he had grown up among them, and they allowed that what he had said was in the manner of jest and not seriousness. So they asked him: ﴿Have you come to us with the truth, or are you among the players?﴾ The pronoun in "they said" refers to his father and his people. "With the truth" is connected to their words "Have you come to us". They did not mean the literal act of coming, because he had not been absent from them and then come to them. This is like ﴿He said: "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 30]. Here "truth" is the opposite of falsehood, meaning seriousness. For this reason they set it against play. The sentence came in nominal form because it is more emphatic, as though they had judged him to be a player and a joker in what he said to them, and also for the sake of the closing rhyme (*fasila*).

Then he turned away from their words and informed them of the seriousness: that the owner of them and the one deserving worship is their Lord, and the Lord of this upper world and this lower world which includes you and your idols. He drew attention to what requires worship, which is the One who originated this world and brought it into existence from pure non-existence. The apparent reading is that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the heavens and the earth. Since the heavens and the earth do not reach a large number, the pronoun used is the pronoun of few (*damir al-qilla*). It has also been said that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the images. Al-Zamakhshari said: "That it refers to the images is more effective for misleading them and more firm for arguing against them." End of quote. Ibn 'Atiyya said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ is an expression for them as if they understood, in that they have obedience and submission, and they have been described in several places with what is described of those who understand." Another said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ refers back with the pronoun of those who understand, because of the states that proceed from them which indicate that they belong to the category of those who understand. Indeed God said: ﴿They said: We come obediently﴾ [Fussilat: 11], and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The heaven creaked, and it has a right to creak.'" End of quote.

It seems that Ibn 'Atiyya and this speaker imagined that *hunna* is among the pronouns specific to feminine things that understand, but this is not so. Rather it is a shared term between those that understand and feminine plural things that do not understand. An example is His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36], where the pronoun refers to the four sacred months.

The indication in ﴿That is your [Lord]﴾ refers to His lordship and His being described as the Originator of this world. The word "from" (*min*) is partitive: that is, of those who testify to lordship there are many, and I am one of them. That is, what I have said is a settled matter upon which there are many witnesses, so it is a statement validated by witnesses. The phrase ﴿upon that﴾ is connected to an omitted element, its estimate being "and I am a witness" ﴿upon that, among the witnesses﴾. Or it is in the sense of explanation, that is, "I mean upon that". Or it is by the active participle, even though it is within the relative clause of *al* (the definite article), because of the breadth in their use of the adverbial and prepositional phrase. There are views on this that were already mentioned under ﴿Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisers﴾ [al-A'raf: 21].

He first hastened to them with a statement that alerts to the indication of reason, but they did not benefit from the statement. So he moved on to a statement that indicates action, which ends in a complete indication of the lack of benefit in the expression of what is subjected to breaking and cutting. It neither repels nor harms nor benefits, and it does not perceive what has happened to it of the dismantling of its parts. So he said: ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols﴾.

The majority read ﴿And by God﴾ with *ta'* (the letter ت). Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Ahmad ibn Hanbal read *bi-Allah* with a single *ba'* (ب) below. Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what is the difference between *ta'* and *ba'*? I answer: *ba'* is the origin, and *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* which was itself substituted for it. The *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, as though he wondered at how easily the plot was accomplished at his hand and by his effort, because that was considered something hopeless due to its difficulty and impossibility. By my life, the like of it is difficult and impossible in every age, especially in the time of Nimrod, with his arrogance, his haughtiness, the strength of his authority, and his zeal in defending his religion. But—"

*"When God ties together a matter's knot, it is made easy."*

End of quote. As for his statement that *ba'* is the origin: it was an origin because it is the broadest of the particles of oath, since it enters upon both nouns and pronouns, is used with the explicit verb of swearing, and may be omitted [p. 322]. As for the claim that *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* of oath, which itself was substituted for the *ba'* of oath, this is something many grammarians have said, but no evidence supports it. Al-Suhayli advanced this view. What analysis requires is that none of them is the origin of another. As for his statement that *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, the explicit statements of the grammarians hold that *ta'* may be accompanied by wonder and may not; the *lam* is what necessarily carries wonder in oaths.

Plotting (*kayd*) is scheming to bring harm upon the target. The apparent reading is that he addressed this sentence to his father and his people, and that it falls under the "he said" in His words ﴿He said: "Rather, your Lord..."﴾. It has been said that he said this secretly from his people, and that one man heard it. It has also been said that a group of their weaker members heard it, those who were walking at the back of the people on the day they went out to the festival. The idols were seventy, and it has been said seventy-two.

The majority read ﴿they turned away, retreating﴾ as the imperfect of *wallā* (to turn away). 'Isa ibn 'Umar read *tuwallu* by dropping one of the two *ta'*s, the second one according to the school of the Basrans, and the first one according to the school of Hisham. This is the imperfect of *tawallā* (to turn oneself away), and it agrees with His saying ﴿so they turned away from him, retreating﴾ [al-Saffat: 90]. The object of "they turned away" is omitted, its meaning being "to your festival".

It is narrated that Azar took him out on one of their festival days. They began with the house of the idols, entered it, prostrated to them, and placed food between them which they had brought with them. They said: "The blessing of the gods will not return to our food." Then they left. When he was on the road, he turned his intention away from going with them, sat down, and said: "I am sick." Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim was from a household that studied the stars, and when they went out to their festival, they would leave none behind except the sick. So Ibrahim came to them with what they were in, and he looked at the sky before the day of the festival and said to his companions: "I am ailing tomorrow." He woke up with his head bound. So they went out and none remained behind except him. He said ﴿And by God, I will surely plot...﴾ to the end. A man heard him, remembered it, and then reported it, and so it spread. End of quote.

There is an omission in the speech, its estimate being: "they turned away to their festival, and Ibrahim came to the idols." ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Debris." Al-Dahhak said: "He took from each pair a limb." It has also been said: the idols were arranged in rows, and among them there was a great idol facing the door, made of gold, with two shining jewels in its eyes. He broke them all with an axe except that great idol, and he hung the axe around its neck. It has been said that he hung it in its hand.

The majority read *judhadhan* (فجُذاذًا) with a *damma* on the *jim*. Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Miqsam, Abu Haywa, Humayd, and al-A'mash in one narration read it with a *kasra*. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Nahik and Abu al-Sammak read it with a *fatha*. These are dialects, the best of which is the *damma*, like *hutham* and *rufat* (debris and crumbs), as Abu Hatim said. Al-Yazidi said: *judhadhan* with a *damma* is the plural of *judhadha*, like *zujaj* and *zujaja* (glass). It has been said that with a *kasra* it is the plural of *jadhid*, like *karim* and *kiram*. It has been said that the *fatha* is a verbal noun, like *al-hasad* (the harvest) in the sense of "the harvested", so the meaning is "cut to pieces". Qutrub said, regarding its three dialects, that it is a verbal noun which is not dualised or pluralised. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *judhadha* with two *damma*s, the plural of *jadhid*, like *jadid* and *judud*. It was also read *judhadhan* with a *damma* on the *jim* and a *fatha* on the *dhal*, lightened, from a verb like *sururun* in *sururun* (the plural of *sarir*, bed), which is a dialect of the tribe of Kalb. Or it is the plural of *juddha*, like *qubba* and *qubab* (dome and domes).

He used the pronoun for those who understand in His saying ﴿so He made them﴾, since they were worshipped. His saying ﴿except a great one among them﴾ is an exception from the pronoun in ﴿so He made them﴾, meaning he did not break it. The pronoun in "among them" may refer to the idols, or to their worshippers. "Great" here means its huge body, or that it was great in standing among them, since they had made it of gold and placed in its eyes two jewels that shine at night. The pronoun in "to it" refers to Ibrahim, meaning he did this with the hope that they would return to him and to his law. Al-Zamakhshari said: "He spared the great one only because it was most likely in his estimation that they would not return except to it, given what they had heard of his denial of their religion and his reviling of their gods, so he would rebuke them with the answer he gave, ﴿Rather, their great one did it; so ask them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63]." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "It is possible that it refers to the great one who was left, but the hope expressed in the sentence weakens this." End of quote.

This is the view of al-Kalbi. Al-Zamakhshari said: "The meaning of this is: perhaps they will return to it, as one returns to a scholar to resolve problems, so they would say, 'What is wrong with these, broken, and with you, intact, with the axe on your shoulder?'" He said: "This is built on his assumption about them, because of what he had tested and experienced of their obstinacy against their reason, their belief in their idols, and their veneration of them; or he said it knowing that they would not return to him, mocking them and calling them fools. The standard for one who is prostrated to and made eligible for worship is that one should be returned to in resolving difficulties." "If you ask: if they returned to the idol through their obstinacy against their reason and the entrenchment of polytheism in their roots, then what religious benefit is there in their returning to it, such that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would make it his aim?" I answer: "If they returned to it, it would become clear that it is powerless, neither benefiting nor harming, and it would be evident that they were in a great matter in worshipping it."

(p. 318)﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾ ﴿They said, "Who has done this to our gods? He is surely among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 59] ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60] ﴿They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 61] ﴿They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 62] ﴿He said, "Rather, this one, their chief, did it. So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63] ﴿So they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 64] ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads: "You know well that these do not speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 65] ﴿He said, "Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 66] ﴿"Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not reason?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 67] ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 68] ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69] ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 70] ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 71] ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made each of them righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72] ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah, and they were worshippers of Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73] ﴿And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that used to commit wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 74] ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 75] ﴿And Noah, when he called out before; so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76] ﴿And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 77] ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field into which the sheep of a people had strayed at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78] ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with David, and the birds too, and We were the doers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 79] ﴿And We taught him the making of armor for you, to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 80] ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, running by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 81] ﴿And among the devils were those who dove for him and did other work besides that. And We were its guardians.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 82] ﴿And Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 83] ﴿So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity, and We gave him his family and the like thereof with them, as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 84] ﴿And Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl, each of them was among the patient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 85] ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 86] ﴿And Dhun-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree against him, then called out in the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87] ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 88] ﴿And Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 89] ﴿So We responded to him, gave him John, and made his wife fit for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, call upon Us in hope and fear, and were humbly submissive to Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90] ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91] ﴿Indeed, this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 92] ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects; each to Us will be returning.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 93] ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We are recording it for him.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 94] ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a city which We have destroyed that they will not return.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95] ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they will be swarming from every elevation.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 96] ﴿And the true promise has drawn near, and at once the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror. "O woe to us! We were in heedlessness of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 97] ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving thereto.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98] ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, but all will abide therein eternally.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 99] ﴿For them therein is a groaning, and they will not hear therein.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 100] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101] ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide eternally in what their souls desire.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 102] ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying, "This is your day, which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103] ﴿On the day We will fold up the heaven like the rolling up of the written scroll for documents. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will be doing it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104] ﴿And We had certainly written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105] ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 106] ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107] ﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God, so will you submit?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108] ﴿And if they turn away, say, "I have announced to you equally, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or distant."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109] ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and knows what you conceal.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 110] ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 111] ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you describe."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 112]

al-Timthal: the made image, a form resembling one of Allah's created beings. One says "mathaltu al-shay' bi al-shay'" when one likens one thing to another. The poet said:

"And how many a day have I spent in pleasure, and a night, with a maiden whose slender form was like the line of a statue."

Al-Jadhdh: cutting off. The poet said:

"The sons of al-Muhallab, may Allah cut off their root, have become ashes, leaving neither root nor branch."

Al-Naks: turning a thing over so that its top becomes its bottom. "Nakkasa ra'sahu," with shadda or without, means he lowered his head until its top became its bottom. Al-Bard: the verbal noun of barada. It is said, "barrada al-ma' harārat al-jawf yubarriduha" (water cools the heat of the stomach). The poet said:

(p. 319) "He left my she-camel idle among the saddle-camels, and she will cool hearts and make the weepers weep."

Al-Nafsh: the grazing of livestock at night without a shepherd, and the wandering of them by day without a shepherd. Al-Ghawṣ: entering under water to extract what is in it. The poet said:

"Or a Sadafite pearl whose diver is joyful; whenever he sees it, he cries out and prostrates."

Al-Nūn: the fish, plural "ninan." It is also narrated that "al-ninan" precedes it, "al-humr." Al-Farj: it is applied to the free (the front), the male as opposed to the female, and to the rear. The poet said:

"And you, when you turned your back on him, he tightened his rear, raised above the ground and not weak."

Al-Hadab: a raised part of the ground, like a mountain, a mound, a grave, and the like. Al-Nasalan: quick walking with haste. The poet said:

"The wolf's swift pace has become near, when the night grew cold upon it, so it hastened."

Al-Haṣab: firewood in the Abyssinian language. When it is thrown into the fire, before it is thrown it is not called haṣab. It is said: the haṣab is what fire is kindled with. Al-Sijill: the record, the document.

﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾.

When the discourse had preceded regarding the proofs of Tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and the return (ma'ad), He followed that with thirteen prophets, without observing chronological order in mentioning them. He also mentioned some of the trials that many of them endured, all of this as consolation to the Messenger ﷺ, and so that he might take them as an example regarding what befell him from his people.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited ﴿rushdahu﴾ with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the shin. 'Isa al-Thaqafi recited "rashadahu" with a fatha on the ra' and the shin, and he attributed the rushd to Ibrahim, meaning it is the rushd of one like him, which is the rushd of the prophets, and it has a great status. Rushd means prophethood and guidance to the ways of righteousness in religion and worldly affairs. Or both are included under rushd. Or the Sahifah and wisdom, or receiving success in good from childhood. There are five opinions. The object of the preposition is from a deleted antecedent, and it is definite, which is why "qabl" is indeclinable: that is, from before Musa and Harun. This was said by al-Dahhak, like His saying in al-An'am: ﴿And Noah, We guided before﴾ [al-An'am: 84], meaning before Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob. He who went to the view that the implied meaning is "before his reaching puberty," or "before his prophethood," meaning when he was in the loins of Adam and the covenant of the prophets was taken, is a far-fetched view. Or before Muhammad ﷺ, because these are deleted elements with no evidence indicating their deletion, unlike "from before" Musa and Harun, since they were mentioned previously. And its nearness. The pronoun in "bihi" most apparently refers to Ibrahim. It was said: it refers to rushd. Allah, exalted is He, informed that He knew from him wondrous states and marvelous secrets, so He qualified him for His intimate friendship (khullah), like His saying: "Allah knows best where to place His messages." This is one of the greatest and most eloquent praises, since Allah, exalted is He, informed that He gave him rushd and that He knew what He had given him, upon him be peace.

Then he digressed from that to explaining rushd, which is calling to the oneness of Allah and rejecting what is worshipped besides Him. "Idh" is governed either by "ataynā" or by "rushdahu" and "ʿālimīn," or by a deleted element, meaning: mention the time of his rushd, this moment. He began first with mentioning his father, because he was the most important in his advice and in rescuing him from error. Then he joined "his people" to it, like His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214]. In His saying ﴿What are these statues﴾ there is a belittling of them, a diminishing of their status, and a feigned ignorance about them, despite his knowledge of them and of their veneration by them. In his address to them with "antum" (you) there is contempt for them and a reproach over their wicked conduct. "ʿAkafa" is transitive with "ʿalā," like His saying: ﴿They cling to idols they have﴾ [al-A'raf: 138]. So it was said that "la-hā" here means "ʿalay-hā," as it was said in His saying: ﴿And if you do evil, it is to yourselves﴾ [al-Isra': 7]. The apparent meaning is that the lam in "la-hā" is the lam of causation, meaning "for its veneration," and the complement of ﴿ʿākifūn﴾ is deleted, meaning "upon its worship." It was said: ʿākifūn has been made to imply the meaning of ʿābidūn, so it takes the lam.
