Al-Zamakhshari said: He did not intend a deleted object for "al-ʿākifīn," and he treated it as an intransitive verb, like His saying "fāʿilūn al-ʿukūf lahā" (doers of the devotion to it), or "wāqifūn lahā" (standing before it). End of quote.

When he questioned them, they answered with mere **taqlid** (blind imitation, *taqlid* being the uncritical following of others) and said that it was the practice of their fathers, so they followed it without any proof. How ugly is this taqlid, which led them to worship wood, stone and metal. Their obstinacy in this matter, and their defence of their imitation, is also clear. His question about worshipping the images had the aim that they would mention some doubt about it, so that he could refute it. When they answered him with something in which they had no doubt-based justification, and their misguidance became evident, ﴿He said: "You and your fathers have certainly been in clear error."﴾ That is, in obvious bewilderment with no ambiguity in it. He judged that both the imitators and those imitated were in error, and he made the error settled for them. The word "you" (*antum*) is an emphatic pronoun for the pronoun that is the subject of "were" (*kana*).

Al-Zamakhshari said: "*Antum* belongs to the kind of emphasis without which the sentence is not sound, because coordinating (*'atf*) upon the pronoun in *huwa* is, in the judgement of the grammarians, like part of the verb, and is therefore impermissible, and similar to it is ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35]." End of quote.

This is not a unanimously agreed ruling, so the sentence is not invalid without it, because the Kufans permit coordinating upon the attached nominative pronoun without emphasis by a detached nominative pronoun and without a separating element. His comparison of this with ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ contradicts his own position on ﴿Dwell, you and your wife﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35], since he claims that "and your wife" is not coordinated upon the concealed pronoun in "dwell" but rather that "and your wife" is nominative by an implied element, meaning "let [your wife] dwell". Thus, according to him, it is a coordination of sentences. This claim contradicts the school of Sibawayh.

When this question and answer had occurred, they were astonished at his misleading them, since he had grown up among them, and they allowed that what he had said was in the manner of jest and not seriousness. So they asked him: ﴿Have you come to us with the truth, or are you among the players?﴾ The pronoun in "they said" refers to his father and his people. "With the truth" is connected to their words "Have you come to us". They did not mean the literal act of coming, because he had not been absent from them and then come to them. This is like ﴿He said: "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 30]. Here "truth" is the opposite of falsehood, meaning seriousness. For this reason they set it against play. The sentence came in nominal form because it is more emphatic, as though they had judged him to be a player and a joker in what he said to them, and also for the sake of the closing rhyme (*fasila*).

Then he turned away from their words and informed them of the seriousness: that the owner of them and the one deserving worship is their Lord, and the Lord of this upper world and this lower world which includes you and your idols. He drew attention to what requires worship, which is the One who originated this world and brought it into existence from pure non-existence. The apparent reading is that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the heavens and the earth. Since the heavens and the earth do not reach a large number, the pronoun used is the pronoun of few (*damir al-qilla*). It has also been said that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the images. Al-Zamakhshari said: "That it refers to the images is more effective for misleading them and more firm for arguing against them." End of quote. Ibn 'Atiyya said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ is an expression for them as if they understood, in that they have obedience and submission, and they have been described in several places with what is described of those who understand." Another said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ refers back with the pronoun of those who understand, because of the states that proceed from them which indicate that they belong to the category of those who understand. Indeed God said: ﴿They said: We come obediently﴾ [Fussilat: 11], and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The heaven creaked, and it has a right to creak.'" End of quote.

It seems that Ibn 'Atiyya and this speaker imagined that *hunna* is among the pronouns specific to feminine things that understand, but this is not so. Rather it is a shared term between those that understand and feminine plural things that do not understand. An example is His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36], where the pronoun refers to the four sacred months.

The indication in ﴿That is your [Lord]﴾ refers to His lordship and His being described as the Originator of this world. The word "from" (*min*) is partitive: that is, of those who testify to lordship there are many, and I am one of them. That is, what I have said is a settled matter upon which there are many witnesses, so it is a statement validated by witnesses. The phrase ﴿upon that﴾ is connected to an omitted element, its estimate being "and I am a witness" ﴿upon that, among the witnesses﴾. Or it is in the sense of explanation, that is, "I mean upon that". Or it is by the active participle, even though it is within the relative clause of *al* (the definite article), because of the breadth in their use of the adverbial and prepositional phrase. There are views on this that were already mentioned under ﴿Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisers﴾ [al-A'raf: 21].

He first hastened to them with a statement that alerts to the indication of reason, but they did not benefit from the statement. So he moved on to a statement that indicates action, which ends in a complete indication of the lack of benefit in the expression of what is subjected to breaking and cutting. It neither repels nor harms nor benefits, and it does not perceive what has happened to it of the dismantling of its parts. So he said: ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols﴾.

The majority read ﴿And by God﴾ with *ta'* (the letter ت). Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Ahmad ibn Hanbal read *bi-Allah* with a single *ba'* (ب) below. Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what is the difference between *ta'* and *ba'*? I answer: *ba'* is the origin, and *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* which was itself substituted for it. The *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, as though he wondered at how easily the plot was accomplished at his hand and by his effort, because that was considered something hopeless due to its difficulty and impossibility. By my life, the like of it is difficult and impossible in every age, especially in the time of Nimrod, with his arrogance, his haughtiness, the strength of his authority, and his zeal in defending his religion. But—"

*"When God ties together a matter's knot, it is made easy."*

End of quote. As for his statement that *ba'* is the origin: it was an origin because it is the broadest of the particles of oath, since it enters upon both nouns and pronouns, is used with the explicit verb of swearing, and may be omitted [p. 322]. As for the claim that *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* of oath, which itself was substituted for the *ba'* of oath, this is something many grammarians have said, but no evidence supports it. Al-Suhayli advanced this view. What analysis requires is that none of them is the origin of another. As for his statement that *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, the explicit statements of the grammarians hold that *ta'* may be accompanied by wonder and may not; the *lam* is what necessarily carries wonder in oaths.

Plotting (*kayd*) is scheming to bring harm upon the target. The apparent reading is that he addressed this sentence to his father and his people, and that it falls under the "he said" in His words ﴿He said: "Rather, your Lord..."﴾. It has been said that he said this secretly from his people, and that one man heard it. It has also been said that a group of their weaker members heard it, those who were walking at the back of the people on the day they went out to the festival. The idols were seventy, and it has been said seventy-two.

The majority read ﴿they turned away, retreating﴾ as the imperfect of *wallā* (to turn away). 'Isa ibn 'Umar read *tuwallu* by dropping one of the two *ta'*s, the second one according to the school of the Basrans, and the first one according to the school of Hisham. This is the imperfect of *tawallā* (to turn oneself away), and it agrees with His saying ﴿so they turned away from him, retreating﴾ [al-Saffat: 90]. The object of "they turned away" is omitted, its meaning being "to your festival".

It is narrated that Azar took him out on one of their festival days. They began with the house of the idols, entered it, prostrated to them, and placed food between them which they had brought with them. They said: "The blessing of the gods will not return to our food." Then they left. When he was on the road, he turned his intention away from going with them, sat down, and said: "I am sick." Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim was from a household that studied the stars, and when they went out to their festival, they would leave none behind except the sick. So Ibrahim came to them with what they were in, and he looked at the sky before the day of the festival and said to his companions: "I am ailing tomorrow." He woke up with his head bound. So they went out and none remained behind except him. He said ﴿And by God, I will surely plot...﴾ to the end. A man heard him, remembered it, and then reported it, and so it spread. End of quote.

There is an omission in the speech, its estimate being: "they turned away to their festival, and Ibrahim came to the idols." ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Debris." Al-Dahhak said: "He took from each pair a limb." It has also been said: the idols were arranged in rows, and among them there was a great idol facing the door, made of gold, with two shining jewels in its eyes. He broke them all with an axe except that great idol, and he hung the axe around its neck. It has been said that he hung it in its hand.

The majority read *judhadhan* (فجُذاذًا) with a *damma* on the *jim*. Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Miqsam, Abu Haywa, Humayd, and al-A'mash in one narration read it with a *kasra*. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Nahik and Abu al-Sammak read it with a *fatha*. These are dialects, the best of which is the *damma*, like *hutham* and *rufat* (debris and crumbs), as Abu Hatim said. Al-Yazidi said: *judhadhan* with a *damma* is the plural of *judhadha*, like *zujaj* and *zujaja* (glass). It has been said that with a *kasra* it is the plural of *jadhid*, like *karim* and *kiram*. It has been said that the *fatha* is a verbal noun, like *al-hasad* (the harvest) in the sense of "the harvested", so the meaning is "cut to pieces". Qutrub said, regarding its three dialects, that it is a verbal noun which is not dualised or pluralised. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *judhadha* with two *damma*s, the plural of *jadhid*, like *jadid* and *judud*. It was also read *judhadhan* with a *damma* on the *jim* and a *fatha* on the *dhal*, lightened, from a verb like *sururun* in *sururun* (the plural of *sarir*, bed), which is a dialect of the tribe of Kalb. Or it is the plural of *juddha*, like *qubba* and *qubab* (dome and domes).

He used the pronoun for those who understand in His saying ﴿so He made them﴾, since they were worshipped. His saying ﴿except a great one among them﴾ is an exception from the pronoun in ﴿so He made them﴾, meaning he did not break it. The pronoun in "among them" may refer to the idols, or to their worshippers. "Great" here means its huge body, or that it was great in standing among them, since they had made it of gold and placed in its eyes two jewels that shine at night. The pronoun in "to it" refers to Ibrahim, meaning he did this with the hope that they would return to him and to his law. Al-Zamakhshari said: "He spared the great one only because it was most likely in his estimation that they would not return except to it, given what they had heard of his denial of their religion and his reviling of their gods, so he would rebuke them with the answer he gave, ﴿Rather, their great one did it; so ask them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63]." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "It is possible that it refers to the great one who was left, but the hope expressed in the sentence weakens this." End of quote.

This is the view of al-Kalbi. Al-Zamakhshari said: "The meaning of this is: perhaps they will return to it, as one returns to a scholar to resolve problems, so they would say, 'What is wrong with these, broken, and with you, intact, with the axe on your shoulder?'" He said: "This is built on his assumption about them, because of what he had tested and experienced of their obstinacy against their reason, their belief in their idols, and their veneration of them; or he said it knowing that they would not return to him, mocking them and calling them fools. The standard for one who is prostrated to and made eligible for worship is that one should be returned to in resolving difficulties." "If you ask: if they returned to the idol through their obstinacy against their reason and the entrenchment of polytheism in their roots, then what religious benefit is there in their returning to it, such that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would make it his aim?" I answer: "If they returned to it, it would become clear that it is powerless, neither benefiting nor harming, and it would be evident that they were in a great matter in worshipping it."

(p. 318)﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾ ﴿They said, "Who has done this to our gods? He is surely among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 59] ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60] ﴿They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 61] ﴿They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 62] ﴿He said, "Rather, this one, their chief, did it. So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63] ﴿So they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 64] ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads: "You know well that these do not speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 65] ﴿He said, "Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 66] ﴿"Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not reason?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 67] ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 68] ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69] ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 70] ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 71] ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made each of them righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72] ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah, and they were worshippers of Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73] ﴿And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that used to commit wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 74] ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 75] ﴿And Noah, when he called out before; so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76] ﴿And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 77] ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field into which the sheep of a people had strayed at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78] ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with David, and the birds too, and We were the doers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 79] ﴿And We taught him the making of armor for you, to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 80] ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, running by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 81] ﴿And among the devils were those who dove for him and did other work besides that. And We were its guardians.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 82] ﴿And Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 83] ﴿So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity, and We gave him his family and the like thereof with them, as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 84] ﴿And Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl, each of them was among the patient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 85] ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 86] ﴿And Dhun-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree against him, then called out in the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87] ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 88] ﴿And Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 89] ﴿So We responded to him, gave him John, and made his wife fit for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, call upon Us in hope and fear, and were humbly submissive to Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90] ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91] ﴿Indeed, this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 92] ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects; each to Us will be returning.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 93] ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We are recording it for him.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 94] ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a city which We have destroyed that they will not return.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95] ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they will be swarming from every elevation.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 96] ﴿And the true promise has drawn near, and at once the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror. "O woe to us! We were in heedlessness of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 97] ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving thereto.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98] ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, but all will abide therein eternally.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 99] ﴿For them therein is a groaning, and they will not hear therein.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 100] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101] ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide eternally in what their souls desire.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 102] ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying, "This is your day, which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103] ﴿On the day We will fold up the heaven like the rolling up of the written scroll for documents. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will be doing it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104] ﴿And We had certainly written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105] ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 106] ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107] ﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God, so will you submit?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108] ﴿And if they turn away, say, "I have announced to you equally, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or distant."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109] ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and knows what you conceal.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 110] ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 111] ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you describe."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 112]

al-Timthal: the made image, a form resembling one of Allah's created beings. One says "mathaltu al-shay' bi al-shay'" when one likens one thing to another. The poet said:

"And how many a day have I spent in pleasure, and a night, with a maiden whose slender form was like the line of a statue."

Al-Jadhdh: cutting off. The poet said:

"The sons of al-Muhallab, may Allah cut off their root, have become ashes, leaving neither root nor branch."

Al-Naks: turning a thing over so that its top becomes its bottom. "Nakkasa ra'sahu," with shadda or without, means he lowered his head until its top became its bottom. Al-Bard: the verbal noun of barada. It is said, "barrada al-ma' harārat al-jawf yubarriduha" (water cools the heat of the stomach). The poet said:

(p. 319) "He left my she-camel idle among the saddle-camels, and she will cool hearts and make the weepers weep."

Al-Nafsh: the grazing of livestock at night without a shepherd, and the wandering of them by day without a shepherd. Al-Ghawṣ: entering under water to extract what is in it. The poet said:

"Or a Sadafite pearl whose diver is joyful; whenever he sees it, he cries out and prostrates."

Al-Nūn: the fish, plural "ninan." It is also narrated that "al-ninan" precedes it, "al-humr." Al-Farj: it is applied to the free (the front), the male as opposed to the female, and to the rear. The poet said:

"And you, when you turned your back on him, he tightened his rear, raised above the ground and not weak."

Al-Hadab: a raised part of the ground, like a mountain, a mound, a grave, and the like. Al-Nasalan: quick walking with haste. The poet said:

"The wolf's swift pace has become near, when the night grew cold upon it, so it hastened."

Al-Haṣab: firewood in the Abyssinian language. When it is thrown into the fire, before it is thrown it is not called haṣab. It is said: the haṣab is what fire is kindled with. Al-Sijill: the record, the document.

﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾.

When the discourse had preceded regarding the proofs of Tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and the return (ma'ad), He followed that with thirteen prophets, without observing chronological order in mentioning them. He also mentioned some of the trials that many of them endured, all of this as consolation to the Messenger ﷺ, and so that he might take them as an example regarding what befell him from his people.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited ﴿rushdahu﴾ with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the shin. 'Isa al-Thaqafi recited "rashadahu" with a fatha on the ra' and the shin, and he attributed the rushd to Ibrahim, meaning it is the rushd of one like him, which is the rushd of the prophets, and it has a great status. Rushd means prophethood and guidance to the ways of righteousness in religion and worldly affairs. Or both are included under rushd. Or the Sahifah and wisdom, or receiving success in good from childhood. There are five opinions. The object of the preposition is from a deleted antecedent, and it is definite, which is why "qabl" is indeclinable: that is, from before Musa and Harun. This was said by al-Dahhak, like His saying in al-An'am: ﴿And Noah, We guided before﴾ [al-An'am: 84], meaning before Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob. He who went to the view that the implied meaning is "before his reaching puberty," or "before his prophethood," meaning when he was in the loins of Adam and the covenant of the prophets was taken, is a far-fetched view. Or before Muhammad ﷺ, because these are deleted elements with no evidence indicating their deletion, unlike "from before" Musa and Harun, since they were mentioned previously. And its nearness. The pronoun in "bihi" most apparently refers to Ibrahim. It was said: it refers to rushd. Allah, exalted is He, informed that He knew from him wondrous states and marvelous secrets, so He qualified him for His intimate friendship (khullah), like His saying: "Allah knows best where to place His messages." This is one of the greatest and most eloquent praises, since Allah, exalted is He, informed that He gave him rushd and that He knew what He had given him, upon him be peace.

Then he digressed from that to explaining rushd, which is calling to the oneness of Allah and rejecting what is worshipped besides Him. "Idh" is governed either by "ataynā" or by "rushdahu" and "ʿālimīn," or by a deleted element, meaning: mention the time of his rushd, this moment. He began first with mentioning his father, because he was the most important in his advice and in rescuing him from error. Then he joined "his people" to it, like His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214]. In His saying ﴿What are these statues﴾ there is a belittling of them, a diminishing of their status, and a feigned ignorance about them, despite his knowledge of them and of their veneration by them. In his address to them with "antum" (you) there is contempt for them and a reproach over their wicked conduct. "ʿAkafa" is transitive with "ʿalā," like His saying: ﴿They cling to idols they have﴾ [al-A'raf: 138]. So it was said that "la-hā" here means "ʿalay-hā," as it was said in His saying: ﴿And if you do evil, it is to yourselves﴾ [al-Isra': 7]. The apparent meaning is that the lam in "la-hā" is the lam of causation, meaning "for its veneration," and the complement of ﴿ʿākifūn﴾ is deleted, meaning "upon its worship." It was said: ʿākifūn has been made to imply the meaning of ʿābidūn, so it takes the lam.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He did not intend a deleted object for "al-ʿākifīn," and he treated it as an intransitive verb, like His saying "fāʿilūn al-ʿukūf lahā" (doers of the devotion to it), or "wāqifūn lahā" (standing before it). End of quote.

When he questioned them, they answered with mere **taqlid** (blind imitation, *taqlid* being the uncritical following of others) and said that it was the practice of their fathers, so they followed it without any proof. How ugly is this taqlid, which led them to worship wood, stone and metal. Their obstinacy in this matter, and their defence of their imitation, is also clear. His question about worshipping the images had the aim that they would mention some doubt about it, so that he could refute it. When they answered him with something in which they had no doubt-based justification, and their misguidance became evident, ﴿He said: "You and your fathers have certainly been in clear error."﴾ That is, in obvious bewilderment with no ambiguity in it. He judged that both the imitators and those imitated were in error, and he made the error settled for them. The word "you" (*antum*) is an emphatic pronoun for the pronoun that is the subject of "were" (*kana*).

Al-Zamakhshari said: "*Antum* belongs to the kind of emphasis without which the sentence is not sound, because coordinating (*'atf*) upon the pronoun in *huwa* is, in the judgement of the grammarians, like part of the verb, and is therefore impermissible, and similar to it is ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35]." End of quote.

This is not a unanimously agreed ruling, so the sentence is not invalid without it, because the Kufans permit coordinating upon the attached nominative pronoun without emphasis by a detached nominative pronoun and without a separating element. His comparison of this with ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ contradicts his own position on ﴿Dwell, you and your wife﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35], since he claims that "and your wife" is not coordinated upon the concealed pronoun in "dwell" but rather that "and your wife" is nominative by an implied element, meaning "let [your wife] dwell". Thus, according to him, it is a coordination of sentences. This claim contradicts the school of Sibawayh.

When this question and answer had occurred, they were astonished at his misleading them, since he had grown up among them, and they allowed that what he had said was in the manner of jest and not seriousness. So they asked him: ﴿Have you come to us with the truth, or are you among the players?﴾ The pronoun in "they said" refers to his father and his people. "With the truth" is connected to their words "Have you come to us". They did not mean the literal act of coming, because he had not been absent from them and then come to them. This is like ﴿He said: "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 30]. Here "truth" is the opposite of falsehood, meaning seriousness. For this reason they set it against play. The sentence came in nominal form because it is more emphatic, as though they had judged him to be a player and a joker in what he said to them, and also for the sake of the closing rhyme (*fasila*).

Then he turned away from their words and informed them of the seriousness: that the owner of them and the one deserving worship is their Lord, and the Lord of this upper world and this lower world which includes you and your idols. He drew attention to what requires worship, which is the One who originated this world and brought it into existence from pure non-existence. The apparent reading is that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the heavens and the earth. Since the heavens and the earth do not reach a large number, the pronoun used is the pronoun of few (*damir al-qilla*). It has also been said that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the images. Al-Zamakhshari said: "That it refers to the images is more effective for misleading them and more firm for arguing against them." End of quote. Ibn 'Atiyya said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ is an expression for them as if they understood, in that they have obedience and submission, and they have been described in several places with what is described of those who understand." Another said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ refers back with the pronoun of those who understand, because of the states that proceed from them which indicate that they belong to the category of those who understand. Indeed God said: ﴿They said: We come obediently﴾ [Fussilat: 11], and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The heaven creaked, and it has a right to creak.'" End of quote.

It seems that Ibn 'Atiyya and this speaker imagined that *hunna* is among the pronouns specific to feminine things that understand, but this is not so. Rather it is a shared term between those that understand and feminine plural things that do not understand. An example is His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36], where the pronoun refers to the four sacred months.

The indication in ﴿That is your [Lord]﴾ refers to His lordship and His being described as the Originator of this world. The word "from" (*min*) is partitive: that is, of those who testify to lordship there are many, and I am one of them. That is, what I have said is a settled matter upon which there are many witnesses, so it is a statement validated by witnesses. The phrase ﴿upon that﴾ is connected to an omitted element, its estimate being "and I am a witness" ﴿upon that, among the witnesses﴾. Or it is in the sense of explanation, that is, "I mean upon that". Or it is by the active participle, even though it is within the relative clause of *al* (the definite article), because of the breadth in their use of the adverbial and prepositional phrase. There are views on this that were already mentioned under ﴿Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisers﴾ [al-A'raf: 21].

He first hastened to them with a statement that alerts to the indication of reason, but they did not benefit from the statement. So he moved on to a statement that indicates action, which ends in a complete indication of the lack of benefit in the expression of what is subjected to breaking and cutting. It neither repels nor harms nor benefits, and it does not perceive what has happened to it of the dismantling of its parts. So he said: ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols﴾.

The majority read ﴿And by God﴾ with *ta'* (the letter ت). Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Ahmad ibn Hanbal read *bi-Allah* with a single *ba'* (ب) below. Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what is the difference between *ta'* and *ba'*? I answer: *ba'* is the origin, and *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* which was itself substituted for it. The *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, as though he wondered at how easily the plot was accomplished at his hand and by his effort, because that was considered something hopeless due to its difficulty and impossibility. By my life, the like of it is difficult and impossible in every age, especially in the time of Nimrod, with his arrogance, his haughtiness, the strength of his authority, and his zeal in defending his religion. But—"

*"When God ties together a matter's knot, it is made easy."*

End of quote. As for his statement that *ba'* is the origin: it was an origin because it is the broadest of the particles of oath, since it enters upon both nouns and pronouns, is used with the explicit verb of swearing, and may be omitted [p. 322]. As for the claim that *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* of oath, which itself was substituted for the *ba'* of oath, this is something many grammarians have said, but no evidence supports it. Al-Suhayli advanced this view. What analysis requires is that none of them is the origin of another. As for his statement that *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, the explicit statements of the grammarians hold that *ta'* may be accompanied by wonder and may not; the *lam* is what necessarily carries wonder in oaths.

Plotting (*kayd*) is scheming to bring harm upon the target. The apparent reading is that he addressed this sentence to his father and his people, and that it falls under the "he said" in His words ﴿He said: "Rather, your Lord..."﴾. It has been said that he said this secretly from his people, and that one man heard it. It has also been said that a group of their weaker members heard it, those who were walking at the back of the people on the day they went out to the festival. The idols were seventy, and it has been said seventy-two.

The majority read ﴿they turned away, retreating﴾ as the imperfect of *wallā* (to turn away). 'Isa ibn 'Umar read *tuwallu* by dropping one of the two *ta'*s, the second one according to the school of the Basrans, and the first one according to the school of Hisham. This is the imperfect of *tawallā* (to turn oneself away), and it agrees with His saying ﴿so they turned away from him, retreating﴾ [al-Saffat: 90]. The object of "they turned away" is omitted, its meaning being "to your festival".

It is narrated that Azar took him out on one of their festival days. They began with the house of the idols, entered it, prostrated to them, and placed food between them which they had brought with them. They said: "The blessing of the gods will not return to our food." Then they left. When he was on the road, he turned his intention away from going with them, sat down, and said: "I am sick." Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim was from a household that studied the stars, and when they went out to their festival, they would leave none behind except the sick. So Ibrahim came to them with what they were in, and he looked at the sky before the day of the festival and said to his companions: "I am ailing tomorrow." He woke up with his head bound. So they went out and none remained behind except him. He said ﴿And by God, I will surely plot...﴾ to the end. A man heard him, remembered it, and then reported it, and so it spread. End of quote.

There is an omission in the speech, its estimate being: "they turned away to their festival, and Ibrahim came to the idols." ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Debris." Al-Dahhak said: "He took from each pair a limb." It has also been said: the idols were arranged in rows, and among them there was a great idol facing the door, made of gold, with two shining jewels in its eyes. He broke them all with an axe except that great idol, and he hung the axe around its neck. It has been said that he hung it in its hand.

The majority read *judhadhan* (فجُذاذًا) with a *damma* on the *jim*. Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Miqsam, Abu Haywa, Humayd, and al-A'mash in one narration read it with a *kasra*. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Nahik and Abu al-Sammak read it with a *fatha*. These are dialects, the best of which is the *damma*, like *hutham* and *rufat* (debris and crumbs), as Abu Hatim said. Al-Yazidi said: *judhadhan* with a *damma* is the plural of *judhadha*, like *zujaj* and *zujaja* (glass). It has been said that with a *kasra* it is the plural of *jadhid*, like *karim* and *kiram*. It has been said that the *fatha* is a verbal noun, like *al-hasad* (the harvest) in the sense of "the harvested", so the meaning is "cut to pieces". Qutrub said, regarding its three dialects, that it is a verbal noun which is not dualised or pluralised. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *judhadha* with two *damma*s, the plural of *jadhid*, like *jadid* and *judud*. It was also read *judhadhan* with a *damma* on the *jim* and a *fatha* on the *dhal*, lightened, from a verb like *sururun* in *sururun* (the plural of *sarir*, bed), which is a dialect of the tribe of Kalb. Or it is the plural of *juddha*, like *qubba* and *qubab* (dome and domes).

He used the pronoun for those who understand in His saying ﴿so He made them﴾, since they were worshipped. His saying ﴿except a great one among them﴾ is an exception from the pronoun in ﴿so He made them﴾, meaning he did not break it. The pronoun in "among them" may refer to the idols, or to their worshippers. "Great" here means its huge body, or that it was great in standing among them, since they had made it of gold and placed in its eyes two jewels that shine at night. The pronoun in "to it" refers to Ibrahim, meaning he did this with the hope that they would return to him and to his law. Al-Zamakhshari said: "He spared the great one only because it was most likely in his estimation that they would not return except to it, given what they had heard of his denial of their religion and his reviling of their gods, so he would rebuke them with the answer he gave, ﴿Rather, their great one did it; so ask them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63]." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "It is possible that it refers to the great one who was left, but the hope expressed in the sentence weakens this." End of quote.

This is the view of al-Kalbi. Al-Zamakhshari said: "The meaning of this is: perhaps they will return to it, as one returns to a scholar to resolve problems, so they would say, 'What is wrong with these, broken, and with you, intact, with the axe on your shoulder?'" He said: "This is built on his assumption about them, because of what he had tested and experienced of their obstinacy against their reason, their belief in their idols, and their veneration of them; or he said it knowing that they would not return to him, mocking them and calling them fools. The standard for one who is prostrated to and made eligible for worship is that one should be returned to in resolving difficulties." "If you ask: if they returned to the idol through their obstinacy against their reason and the entrenchment of polytheism in their roots, then what religious benefit is there in their returning to it, such that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would make it his aim?" I answer: "If they returned to it, it would become clear that it is powerless, neither benefiting nor harming, and it would be evident that they were in a great matter in worshipping it."

(p. 318)﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾ ﴿They said, "Who has done this to our gods? He is surely among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 59] ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60] ﴿They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 61] ﴿They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 62] ﴿He said, "Rather, this one, their chief, did it. So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63] ﴿So they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 64] ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads: "You know well that these do not speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 65] ﴿He said, "Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 66] ﴿"Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not reason?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 67] ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 68] ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69] ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 70] ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 71] ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made each of them righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72] ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah, and they were worshippers of Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73] ﴿And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that used to commit wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 74] ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 75] ﴿And Noah, when he called out before; so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76] ﴿And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 77] ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field into which the sheep of a people had strayed at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78] ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with David, and the birds too, and We were the doers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 79] ﴿And We taught him the making of armor for you, to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 80] ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, running by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 81] ﴿And among the devils were those who dove for him and did other work besides that. And We were its guardians.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 82] ﴿And Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 83] ﴿So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity, and We gave him his family and the like thereof with them, as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 84] ﴿And Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl, each of them was among the patient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 85] ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 86] ﴿And Dhun-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree against him, then called out in the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87] ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 88] ﴿And Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 89] ﴿So We responded to him, gave him John, and made his wife fit for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, call upon Us in hope and fear, and were humbly submissive to Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90] ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91] ﴿Indeed, this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 92] ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects; each to Us will be returning.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 93] ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We are recording it for him.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 94] ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a city which We have destroyed that they will not return.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95] ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they will be swarming from every elevation.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 96] ﴿And the true promise has drawn near, and at once the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror. "O woe to us! We were in heedlessness of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 97] ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving thereto.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98] ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, but all will abide therein eternally.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 99] ﴿For them therein is a groaning, and they will not hear therein.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 100] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101] ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide eternally in what their souls desire.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 102] ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying, "This is your day, which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103] ﴿On the day We will fold up the heaven like the rolling up of the written scroll for documents. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will be doing it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104] ﴿And We had certainly written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105] ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 106] ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107] ﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God, so will you submit?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108] ﴿And if they turn away, say, "I have announced to you equally, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or distant."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109] ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and knows what you conceal.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 110] ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 111] ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you describe."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 112]

al-Timthal: the made image, a form resembling one of Allah's created beings. One says "mathaltu al-shay' bi al-shay'" when one likens one thing to another. The poet said:

"And how many a day have I spent in pleasure, and a night, with a maiden whose slender form was like the line of a statue."

Al-Jadhdh: cutting off. The poet said:

"The sons of al-Muhallab, may Allah cut off their root, have become ashes, leaving neither root nor branch."

Al-Naks: turning a thing over so that its top becomes its bottom. "Nakkasa ra'sahu," with shadda or without, means he lowered his head until its top became its bottom. Al-Bard: the verbal noun of barada. It is said, "barrada al-ma' harārat al-jawf yubarriduha" (water cools the heat of the stomach). The poet said:

(p. 319) "He left my she-camel idle among the saddle-camels, and she will cool hearts and make the weepers weep."

Al-Nafsh: the grazing of livestock at night without a shepherd, and the wandering of them by day without a shepherd. Al-Ghawṣ: entering under water to extract what is in it. The poet said:

"Or a Sadafite pearl whose diver is joyful; whenever he sees it, he cries out and prostrates."

Al-Nūn: the fish, plural "ninan." It is also narrated that "al-ninan" precedes it, "al-humr." Al-Farj: it is applied to the free (the front), the male as opposed to the female, and to the rear. The poet said:

"And you, when you turned your back on him, he tightened his rear, raised above the ground and not weak."

Al-Hadab: a raised part of the ground, like a mountain, a mound, a grave, and the like. Al-Nasalan: quick walking with haste. The poet said:

"The wolf's swift pace has become near, when the night grew cold upon it, so it hastened."

Al-Haṣab: firewood in the Abyssinian language. When it is thrown into the fire, before it is thrown it is not called haṣab. It is said: the haṣab is what fire is kindled with. Al-Sijill: the record, the document.

﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾.

When the discourse had preceded regarding the proofs of Tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and the return (ma'ad), He followed that with thirteen prophets, without observing chronological order in mentioning them. He also mentioned some of the trials that many of them endured, all of this as consolation to the Messenger ﷺ, and so that he might take them as an example regarding what befell him from his people.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited ﴿rushdahu﴾ with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the shin. 'Isa al-Thaqafi recited "rashadahu" with a fatha on the ra' and the shin, and he attributed the rushd to Ibrahim, meaning it is the rushd of one like him, which is the rushd of the prophets, and it has a great status. Rushd means prophethood and guidance to the ways of righteousness in religion and worldly affairs. Or both are included under rushd. Or the Sahifah and wisdom, or receiving success in good from childhood. There are five opinions. The object of the preposition is from a deleted antecedent, and it is definite, which is why "qabl" is indeclinable: that is, from before Musa and Harun. This was said by al-Dahhak, like His saying in al-An'am: ﴿And Noah, We guided before﴾ [al-An'am: 84], meaning before Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob. He who went to the view that the implied meaning is "before his reaching puberty," or "before his prophethood," meaning when he was in the loins of Adam and the covenant of the prophets was taken, is a far-fetched view. Or before Muhammad ﷺ, because these are deleted elements with no evidence indicating their deletion, unlike "from before" Musa and Harun, since they were mentioned previously. And its nearness. The pronoun in "bihi" most apparently refers to Ibrahim. It was said: it refers to rushd. Allah, exalted is He, informed that He knew from him wondrous states and marvelous secrets, so He qualified him for His intimate friendship (khullah), like His saying: "Allah knows best where to place His messages." This is one of the greatest and most eloquent praises, since Allah, exalted is He, informed that He gave him rushd and that He knew what He had given him, upon him be peace.

Then he digressed from that to explaining rushd, which is calling to the oneness of Allah and rejecting what is worshipped besides Him. "Idh" is governed either by "ataynā" or by "rushdahu" and "ʿālimīn," or by a deleted element, meaning: mention the time of his rushd, this moment. He began first with mentioning his father, because he was the most important in his advice and in rescuing him from error. Then he joined "his people" to it, like His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214]. In His saying ﴿What are these statues﴾ there is a belittling of them, a diminishing of their status, and a feigned ignorance about them, despite his knowledge of them and of their veneration by them. In his address to them with "antum" (you) there is contempt for them and a reproach over their wicked conduct. "ʿAkafa" is transitive with "ʿalā," like His saying: ﴿They cling to idols they have﴾ [al-A'raf: 138]. So it was said that "la-hā" here means "ʿalay-hā," as it was said in His saying: ﴿And if you do evil, it is to yourselves﴾ [al-Isra': 7]. The apparent meaning is that the lam in "la-hā" is the lam of causation, meaning "for its veneration," and the complement of ﴿ʿākifūn﴾ is deleted, meaning "upon its worship." It was said: ʿākifūn has been made to imply the meaning of ʿābidūn, so it takes the lam.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He did not intend a deleted object for "al-ʿākifīn," and he treated it as an intransitive verb, like His saying "fāʿilūn al-ʿukūf lahā" (doers of the devotion to it), or "wāqifūn lahā" (standing before it). End of quote.

When he questioned them, they answered with mere **taqlid** (blind imitation, *taqlid* being the uncritical following of others) and said that it was the practice of their fathers, so they followed it without any proof. How ugly is this taqlid, which led them to worship wood, stone and metal. Their obstinacy in this matter, and their defence of their imitation, is also clear. His question about worshipping the images had the aim that they would mention some doubt about it, so that he could refute it. When they answered him with something in which they had no doubt-based justification, and their misguidance became evident, ﴿He said: "You and your fathers have certainly been in clear error."﴾ That is, in obvious bewilderment with no ambiguity in it. He judged that both the imitators and those imitated were in error, and he made the error settled for them. The word "you" (*antum*) is an emphatic pronoun for the pronoun that is the subject of "were" (*kana*).

Al-Zamakhshari said: "*Antum* belongs to the kind of emphasis without which the sentence is not sound, because coordinating (*'atf*) upon the pronoun in *huwa* is, in the judgement of the grammarians, like part of the verb, and is therefore impermissible, and similar to it is ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35]." End of quote.

This is not a unanimously agreed ruling, so the sentence is not invalid without it, because the Kufans permit coordinating upon the attached nominative pronoun without emphasis by a detached nominative pronoun and without a separating element. His comparison of this with ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ contradicts his own position on ﴿Dwell, you and your wife﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35], since he claims that "and your wife" is not coordinated upon the concealed pronoun in "dwell" but rather that "and your wife" is nominative by an implied element, meaning "let [your wife] dwell". Thus, according to him, it is a coordination of sentences. This claim contradicts the school of Sibawayh.

When this question and answer had occurred, they were astonished at his misleading them, since he had grown up among them, and they allowed that what he had said was in the manner of jest and not seriousness. So they asked him: ﴿Have you come to us with the truth, or are you among the players?﴾ The pronoun in "they said" refers to his father and his people. "With the truth" is connected to their words "Have you come to us". They did not mean the literal act of coming, because he had not been absent from them and then come to them. This is like ﴿He said: "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 30]. Here "truth" is the opposite of falsehood, meaning seriousness. For this reason they set it against play. The sentence came in nominal form because it is more emphatic, as though they had judged him to be a player and a joker in what he said to them, and also for the sake of the closing rhyme (*fasila*).

Then he turned away from their words and informed them of the seriousness: that the owner of them and the one deserving worship is their Lord, and the Lord of this upper world and this lower world which includes you and your idols. He drew attention to what requires worship, which is the One who originated this world and brought it into existence from pure non-existence. The apparent reading is that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the heavens and the earth. Since the heavens and the earth do not reach a large number, the pronoun used is the pronoun of few (*damir al-qilla*). It has also been said that the pronoun in ﴿who originated them﴾ refers to the images. Al-Zamakhshari said: "That it refers to the images is more effective for misleading them and more firm for arguing against them." End of quote. Ibn 'Atiyya said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ is an expression for them as if they understood, in that they have obedience and submission, and they have been described in several places with what is described of those who understand." Another said: "﴿Who originated them﴾ refers back with the pronoun of those who understand, because of the states that proceed from them which indicate that they belong to the category of those who understand. Indeed God said: ﴿They said: We come obediently﴾ [Fussilat: 11], and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The heaven creaked, and it has a right to creak.'" End of quote.

It seems that Ibn 'Atiyya and this speaker imagined that *hunna* is among the pronouns specific to feminine things that understand, but this is not so. Rather it is a shared term between those that understand and feminine plural things that do not understand. An example is His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36], where the pronoun refers to the four sacred months.

The indication in ﴿That is your [Lord]﴾ refers to His lordship and His being described as the Originator of this world. The word "from" (*min*) is partitive: that is, of those who testify to lordship there are many, and I am one of them. That is, what I have said is a settled matter upon which there are many witnesses, so it is a statement validated by witnesses. The phrase ﴿upon that﴾ is connected to an omitted element, its estimate being "and I am a witness" ﴿upon that, among the witnesses﴾. Or it is in the sense of explanation, that is, "I mean upon that". Or it is by the active participle, even though it is within the relative clause of *al* (the definite article), because of the breadth in their use of the adverbial and prepositional phrase. There are views on this that were already mentioned under ﴿Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisers﴾ [al-A'raf: 21].

He first hastened to them with a statement that alerts to the indication of reason, but they did not benefit from the statement. So he moved on to a statement that indicates action, which ends in a complete indication of the lack of benefit in the expression of what is subjected to breaking and cutting. It neither repels nor harms nor benefits, and it does not perceive what has happened to it of the dismantling of its parts. So he said: ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols﴾.

The majority read ﴿And by God﴾ with *ta'* (the letter ت). Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Ahmad ibn Hanbal read *bi-Allah* with a single *ba'* (ب) below. Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what is the difference between *ta'* and *ba'*? I answer: *ba'* is the origin, and *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* which was itself substituted for it. The *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, as though he wondered at how easily the plot was accomplished at his hand and by his effort, because that was considered something hopeless due to its difficulty and impossibility. By my life, the like of it is difficult and impossible in every age, especially in the time of Nimrod, with his arrogance, his haughtiness, the strength of his authority, and his zeal in defending his religion. But—"

*"When God ties together a matter's knot, it is made easy."*

End of quote. As for his statement that *ba'* is the origin: it was an origin because it is the broadest of the particles of oath, since it enters upon both nouns and pronouns, is used with the explicit verb of swearing, and may be omitted [p. 322]. As for the claim that *ta'* is a substitute for the *waw* of oath, which itself was substituted for the *ba'* of oath, this is something many grammarians have said, but no evidence supports it. Al-Suhayli advanced this view. What analysis requires is that none of them is the origin of another. As for his statement that *ta'* carries an extra meaning, which is wonder, the explicit statements of the grammarians hold that *ta'* may be accompanied by wonder and may not; the *lam* is what necessarily carries wonder in oaths.

Plotting (*kayd*) is scheming to bring harm upon the target. The apparent reading is that he addressed this sentence to his father and his people, and that it falls under the "he said" in His words ﴿He said: "Rather, your Lord..."﴾. It has been said that he said this secretly from his people, and that one man heard it. It has also been said that a group of their weaker members heard it, those who were walking at the back of the people on the day they went out to the festival. The idols were seventy, and it has been said seventy-two.

The majority read ﴿they turned away, retreating﴾ as the imperfect of *wallā* (to turn away). 'Isa ibn 'Umar read *tuwallu* by dropping one of the two *ta'*s, the second one according to the school of the Basrans, and the first one according to the school of Hisham. This is the imperfect of *tawallā* (to turn oneself away), and it agrees with His saying ﴿so they turned away from him, retreating﴾ [al-Saffat: 90]. The object of "they turned away" is omitted, its meaning being "to your festival".

It is narrated that Azar took him out on one of their festival days. They began with the house of the idols, entered it, prostrated to them, and placed food between them which they had brought with them. They said: "The blessing of the gods will not return to our food." Then they left. When he was on the road, he turned his intention away from going with them, sat down, and said: "I am sick." Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim was from a household that studied the stars, and when they went out to their festival, they would leave none behind except the sick. So Ibrahim came to them with what they were in, and he looked at the sky before the day of the festival and said to his companions: "I am ailing tomorrow." He woke up with his head bound. So they went out and none remained behind except him. He said ﴿And by God, I will surely plot...﴾ to the end. A man heard him, remembered it, and then reported it, and so it spread. End of quote.

There is an omission in the speech, its estimate being: "they turned away to their festival, and Ibrahim came to the idols." ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Debris." Al-Dahhak said: "He took from each pair a limb." It has also been said: the idols were arranged in rows, and among them there was a great idol facing the door, made of gold, with two shining jewels in its eyes. He broke them all with an axe except that great idol, and he hung the axe around its neck. It has been said that he hung it in its hand.

The majority read *judhadhan* (فجُذاذًا) with a *damma* on the *jim*. Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Miqsam, Abu Haywa, Humayd, and al-A'mash in one narration read it with a *kasra*. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Nahik and Abu al-Sammak read it with a *fatha*. These are dialects, the best of which is the *damma*, like *hutham* and *rufat* (debris and crumbs), as Abu Hatim said. Al-Yazidi said: *judhadhan* with a *damma* is the plural of *judhadha*, like *zujaj* and *zujaja* (glass). It has been said that with a *kasra* it is the plural of *jadhid*, like *karim* and *kiram*. It has been said that the *fatha* is a verbal noun, like *al-hasad* (the harvest) in the sense of "the harvested", so the meaning is "cut to pieces". Qutrub said, regarding its three dialects, that it is a verbal noun which is not dualised or pluralised. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *judhadha* with two *damma*s, the plural of *jadhid*, like *jadid* and *judud*. It was also read *judhadhan* with a *damma* on the *jim* and a *fatha* on the *dhal*, lightened, from a verb like *sururun* in *sururun* (the plural of *sarir*, bed), which is a dialect of the tribe of Kalb. Or it is the plural of *juddha*, like *qubba* and *qubab* (dome and domes).

He used the pronoun for those who understand in His saying ﴿so He made them﴾, since they were worshipped. His saying ﴿except a great one among them﴾ is an exception from the pronoun in ﴿so He made them﴾, meaning he did not break it. The pronoun in "among them" may refer to the idols, or to their worshippers. "Great" here means its huge body, or that it was great in standing among them, since they had made it of gold and placed in its eyes two jewels that shine at night. The pronoun in "to it" refers to Ibrahim, meaning he did this with the hope that they would return to him and to his law. Al-Zamakhshari said: "He spared the great one only because it was most likely in his estimation that they would not return except to it, given what they had heard of his denial of their religion and his reviling of their gods, so he would rebuke them with the answer he gave, ﴿Rather, their great one did it; so ask them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63]." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "It is possible that it refers to the great one who was left, but the hope expressed in the sentence weakens this." End of quote.

This is the view of al-Kalbi. Al-Zamakhshari said: "The meaning of this is: perhaps they will return to it, as one returns to a scholar to resolve problems, so they would say, 'What is wrong with these, broken, and with you, intact, with the axe on your shoulder?'" He said: "This is built on his assumption about them, because of what he had tested and experienced of their obstinacy against their reason, their belief in their idols, and their veneration of them; or he said it knowing that they would not return to him, mocking them and calling them fools. The standard for one who is prostrated to and made eligible for worship is that one should be returned to in resolving difficulties." "If you ask: if they returned to the idol through their obstinacy against their reason and the entrenchment of polytheism in their roots, then what religious benefit is there in their returning to it, such that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would make it his aim?" I answer: "If they returned to it, it would become clear that it is powerless, neither benefiting nor harming, and it would be evident that they were in a great matter in worshipping it."

(p. 318)﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾ ﴿They said, "Who has done this to our gods? He is surely among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 59] ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60] ﴿They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 61] ﴿They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 62] ﴿He said, "Rather, this one, their chief, did it. So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63] ﴿So they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 64] ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads: "You know well that these do not speak."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 65] ﴿He said, "Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 66] ﴿"Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not reason?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 67] ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 68] ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69] ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 70] ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 71] ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made each of them righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72] ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah, and they were worshippers of Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73] ﴿And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that used to commit wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 74] ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 75] ﴿And Noah, when he called out before; so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76] ﴿And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 77] ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field into which the sheep of a people had strayed at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78] ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with David, and the birds too, and We were the doers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 79] ﴿And We taught him the making of armor for you, to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 80] ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, running by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 81] ﴿And among the devils were those who dove for him and did other work besides that. And We were its guardians.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 82] ﴿And Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 83] ﴿So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity, and We gave him his family and the like thereof with them, as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 84] ﴿And Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl, each of them was among the patient.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 85] ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were among the righteous.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 86] ﴿And Dhun-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree against him, then called out in the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87] ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 88] ﴿And Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 89] ﴿So We responded to him, gave him John, and made his wife fit for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, call upon Us in hope and fear, and were humbly submissive to Us.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90] ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91] ﴿Indeed, this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 92] ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects; each to Us will be returning.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 93] ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We are recording it for him.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 94] ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a city which We have destroyed that they will not return.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95] ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they will be swarming from every elevation.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 96] ﴿And the true promise has drawn near, and at once the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror. "O woe to us! We were in heedlessness of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 97] ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving thereto.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98] ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, but all will abide therein eternally.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 99] ﴿For them therein is a groaning, and they will not hear therein.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 100] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101] ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide eternally in what their souls desire.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 102] ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying, "This is your day, which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103] ﴿On the day We will fold up the heaven like the rolling up of the written scroll for documents. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will be doing it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104] ﴿And We had certainly written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105] ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 106] ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107] ﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God, so will you submit?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108] ﴿And if they turn away, say, "I have announced to you equally, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or distant."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109] ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and knows what you conceal.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 110] ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 111] ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you describe."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 112]

al-Timthal: the made image, a form resembling one of Allah's created beings. One says "mathaltu al-shay' bi al-shay'" when one likens one thing to another. The poet said:

"And how many a day have I spent in pleasure, and a night, with a maiden whose slender form was like the line of a statue."

Al-Jadhdh: cutting off. The poet said:

"The sons of al-Muhallab, may Allah cut off their root, have become ashes, leaving neither root nor branch."

Al-Naks: turning a thing over so that its top becomes its bottom. "Nakkasa ra'sahu," with shadda or without, means he lowered his head until its top became its bottom. Al-Bard: the verbal noun of barada. It is said, "barrada al-ma' harārat al-jawf yubarriduha" (water cools the heat of the stomach). The poet said:

(p. 319) "He left my she-camel idle among the saddle-camels, and she will cool hearts and make the weepers weep."

Al-Nafsh: the grazing of livestock at night without a shepherd, and the wandering of them by day without a shepherd. Al-Ghawṣ: entering under water to extract what is in it. The poet said:

"Or a Sadafite pearl whose diver is joyful; whenever he sees it, he cries out and prostrates."

Al-Nūn: the fish, plural "ninan." It is also narrated that "al-ninan" precedes it, "al-humr." Al-Farj: it is applied to the free (the front), the male as opposed to the female, and to the rear. The poet said:

"And you, when you turned your back on him, he tightened his rear, raised above the ground and not weak."

Al-Hadab: a raised part of the ground, like a mountain, a mound, a grave, and the like. Al-Nasalan: quick walking with haste. The poet said:

"The wolf's swift pace has become near, when the night grew cold upon it, so it hastened."

Al-Haṣab: firewood in the Abyssinian language. When it is thrown into the fire, before it is thrown it is not called haṣab. It is said: the haṣab is what fire is kindled with. Al-Sijill: the record, the document.

﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the jesters?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to that.﴾ ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except for a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾.

When the discourse had preceded regarding the proofs of Tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and the return (ma'ad), He followed that with thirteen prophets, without observing chronological order in mentioning them. He also mentioned some of the trials that many of them endured, all of this as consolation to the Messenger ﷺ, and so that he might take them as an example regarding what befell him from his people.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited ﴿rushdahu﴾ with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the shin.
